manualTranslations.zh: 文德元年二月，僖宗自興元還京。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Wende, Emperor Xizong returned to the capital from Xingyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wende 1, Emperor Xizong returned to the capital from Xingyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 三月，僖宗崩，昭宗即位，以武皇為開府儀同三司、檢校太師、兼侍中、隴西郡王，食邑七千戶，食實封二百戶。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month Xizong died and Zhaozong took the throne; Wuhuang was made commissioner with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, honorary Grand Tutor, concurrent Palace Attendant, Duke of Longxi, with a fief of seven thousand households and two hundred enfeoffed households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month Xizong died and Zhaozong succeeded; Wuhuang was made open-office commissioner with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, honorary Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant, and Duke of Longxi, with a fief of seven thousand households and two hundred enfeoffed households.

manualTranslations.zh: 河南尹張全義潛兵夜襲李罕之於河陽，城陷，舉族為全義所擄；
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Quanyi, governor of Henan, secretly sent troops by night to surprise Li Hanzhi at Heyang; the city fell and his whole clan was carried off by Quanyi;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi, Henan governor, sent troops by night to surprise Li Hanzhi at Heyang; the city fell and Quanyi carried off his whole clan;

manualTranslations.zh: 罕之逾垣獲免，遂來歸於武皇。
manualTranslations.literal: Hanzhi climbed over a wall and escaped, then came to submit to Wuhuang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hanzhi climbed a wall and escaped, then came to Wuhuang.

manualTranslations.zh: 遣李存孝、薛阿檀、史儼兒、安金俊、安休休將七千騎送罕之至河陽。
manualTranslations.literal: He sent Li Cunxiao, Xue Atan, Shi Yan'er, An Jinjun, and An Xiuxiu with seven thousand horsemen to escort Hanzhi back to Heyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sent Li Cunxiao, Xue Atan, Shi Yan'er, An Jinjun, and An Xiuxiu with seven thousand horsemen to escort Hanzhi to Heyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 汴將丁會、牛存節、葛從周將兵赴援，李存孝率精騎逆戰於溫縣。
manualTranslations.literal: The Bian generals Ding Hui, Niu Cunjie, and Ge Congzhou led troops to the relief; Li Cunxiao led picked cavalry to meet them in battle at Wen County.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Bian generals Ding Hui, Niu Cunjie, and Ge Congzhou marched to the relief; Li Cunxiao met them with picked cavalry at Wen County.

manualTranslations.zh: 汴人既扼太行之路，存孝殿軍而退。
manualTranslations.literal: The men of Bian having blocked the Taihang route, Cunxiao covered the rear and withdrew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With the Bian forces blocking the Taihang road, Cunxiao covered the retreat and withdrew.

manualTranslations.zh: 騎將安休休以戰不利，奔於蔡。
manualTranslations.literal: The mounted commander An Xiuxiu, because the battle went badly, fled to Cai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The cavalry commander An Xiuxiu, fearing defeat, fled to Cai.

manualTranslations.zh: 武皇以罕之為澤州刺史，遙領河陽節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: Wuhuang made Hanzhi prefect of Ze and titular military commissioner of Heyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wuhuang made Hanzhi prefect of Ze and titular commissioner of Heyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 十月，邢州孟方立遣大將奚忠信將兵三萬寇遼州，武皇大破之，斬首萬級，生擒奚忠信。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth month Meng Fangli of Xing Prefecture sent the great general Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand troops to raid Liaozhou; Wuhuang routed them, beheaded ten thousand, and captured Xi Zhongxin alive.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Meng Fangli of Xingzhou sent Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand troops against Liaozhou; Wuhuang crushed them, took ten thousand heads, and captured Xi Zhongxin alive.

sourceRange.text: 大順元年，遣李存孝攻邢州，孟遷以邢、洺、磁三州降，執汴將王虔裕三百人以獻。武皇徙孟遷於太原，以安金俊為邢洺團練使。三月，昭義軍節度使李克修卒，以李克恭為潞州節度使。是月，武皇攻雲州，拔其東城。赫連鐸求援於燕，燕帥李匡威將兵三萬以赴之，戰於城下，燕軍大敗。時徐州時溥為汴軍所攻，遣使來求援，武皇命石君和由兗、鄆以赴之。

context.beforeSource: 汴將王虔裕率精甲數百入於邢州，罕之等班師。
context.afterSource: 五月，潞州軍亂，殺節度使李克恭，州人推牙將安居受為留後，南結汴將。
context.beforeLocal: 汴將王虔裕率精甲數百入於邢州，罕之等班師。
context.afterLocal: 五月，潞州軍亂，殺節度使李克恭，州人推牙將安居受為留後，南結汴將。

manualTranslations.zh: 大順元年，遣李存孝攻邢州，孟遷以邢、洺、磁三州降，執汴將王虔裕三百人以獻。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Datong, he sent Li Cunxiao to attack Xing Prefecture; Meng Qian surrendered Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures and presented three hundred Bian captives led by Wang Qianyu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Datong 1 he sent Li Cunxiao against Xingzhou; Meng Qian surrendered Xing, Ming, and Cizhou and presented three hundred Bian prisoners led by Wang Qianyu.

manualTranslations.zh: 武皇徙孟遷於太原，以安金俊為邢洺團練使。
manualTranslations.literal: Wuhuang moved Meng Qian to Taiyuan and made An Jinjun regimental commissioner of Xing and Ming.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wuhuang moved Meng Qian to Taiyuan and made An Jinjun regimental commissioner of Xing and Ming.

manualTranslations.zh: 三月，昭義軍節度使李克修卒，以李克恭為潞州節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Kexiu died, and Li Kegong was made military commissioner of Lu Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month Zhaoyi commissioner Li Kexiu died, and Li Kegong was made military commissioner of Luzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 是月，武皇攻雲州，拔其東城。
manualTranslations.literal: That month Wuhuang attacked Yun Prefecture and took its eastern city.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That month Wuhuang attacked Yunzhou and captured its eastern quarter.

manualTranslations.zh: 赫連鐸求援於燕，燕帥李匡威將兵三萬以赴之，戰於城下，燕軍大敗。
manualTranslations.literal: Helian Duo sought aid from Yan; the Yan commander Li Kuangwei led thirty thousand troops to go to the relief; they fought below the walls and the Yan army was routed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Helian Duo appealed to Yan; the Yan commander Li Kuangwei marched thirty thousand men to his aid; they fought below the walls and the Yan army was routed.

manualTranslations.zh: 時徐州時溥為汴軍所攻，遣使來求援，武皇命石君和由兗、鄆以赴之。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Shi Pu of Xuzhou was attacked by the Bian army; he sent envoys begging for aid, and Wuhuang ordered Shi Junhe to go by way of Yan and Yun to the relief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shi Pu of Xuzhou was then under attack by Bian; he sent envoys begging for aid, and Wuhuang ordered Shi Junhe to march from Yan and Yun to relieve him.

sourceRange.text: 光啟元年三月，幽州李可舉、鎮州王景崇連兵寇定州，節度使王處存求援於武皇；武皇遣大將康君立、安老、薛可、郭啜率兵赴之。五月，鎮人攻無極，武皇親領兵救之。鎮人退保新城，武皇攻之，斬首萬餘級，獲馬千匹。王處存亦敗燕軍於易州。

context.beforeSource: 及武皇表至，朝廷大恐，遣內臣宣諭，尋加守太傅、同平章事、隴西郡王。
context.afterSource: 十一月，河中王重榮遣使來乞師，且言邠州朱玫、鳳翔李符將加兵於己。
context.beforeLocal: 及武皇表至，朝廷大恐，遣內臣宣諭，尋加守太傅、同平章事、隴西郡王。

manualTranslations.zh: 光啟元年三月，幽州李可舉、鎮州王景崇連兵寇定州，節度使王處存求援於武皇；
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Guangqi, Li Keju of Youzhou and Wang Jingchong of Zhenzhou jointly marched to raid Ding Prefecture; military commissioner Wang Chucun sought aid from Wuhuang;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month of Guangqi 1, Li Keju of Youzhou and Wang Jingchong of Zhenzhou jointly attacked Ding Prefecture; Wang Chucun, the military commissioner, appealed to Wuhuang for aid;

manualTranslations.zh: 武皇遣大將康君立、安老、薛可、郭啜率兵赴之。
manualTranslations.literal: Wuhuang sent the great generals Kang Junli, An Lao, Xue Ke, and Guo Chuo with troops to go to the relief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wuhuang sent Kang Junli, An Lao, Xue Ke, and Guo Chuo with troops to the rescue.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月，鎮人攻無極，武皇親領兵救之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month the men of Zhen attacked Wuji; Wuhuang personally led troops to the rescue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Zhen troops attacked Wuji; Wuhuang led the army in person to relieve it.

manualTranslations.zh: 鎮人退保新城，武皇攻之，斬首萬餘級，獲馬千匹。
manualTranslations.literal: The men of Zhen fell back to defend Xincheng; Wuhuang attacked them, beheaded more than ten thousand, and captured a thousand horses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zhen troops fell back to Xincheng; Wuhuang stormed the place, took more than ten thousand heads, and seized a thousand horses.

manualTranslations.zh: 王處存亦敗燕軍於易州。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Chucun also defeated the Yan army at Yi Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun also routed the Yan army at Yizhou.

context.afterSource: 四月，汴將葛從周寇邢、洺、磁等州，旬日之內，三州連陷。

manualTranslations.zh: 光化元年春正月，鳳翔李茂貞、華州韓建皆致書於武皇，乞修和好，同獎王室，兼乞助丁匠修繕秦宮，武皇許之。
manualTranslations.literal: First month of spring in Guanghua 1, Li Maozhen of Fengxiang and Han Jian of Huazhou both sent letters to Wuhuang begging to restore good relations, jointly to encourage the royal house, and also begging help with laborers and craftsmen to repair the Qin palace; Wuhuang granted it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of Guanghua 1, Li Maozhen of Fengxiang and Han Jian of Huazhou both wrote Wuhuang seeking peace, pledging to uphold the throne, and asking for craftsmen to repair the Qin palace; Wuhuang agreed.

sourceRange.text: 景福元年正月，鎮州王鎔恃燕人之援，率兵十餘萬攻邢州之堯山。武皇遣李存信將兵應援，李存孝素與存信不協，遞相猜貳，留兵不進。武皇又遣李嗣勳、李存審將兵援之，大破燕、趙之眾，斬首三萬，收其軍實。三月，武皇進軍渡滹沱，攻欒城，下鼓城、槁城。四月，燕軍寇雲、代，武皇班師。

context.afterSource: 八月，赫連鐸誘幽州李匡威之眾八萬，寇天成軍，遂攻雲州，營於州北，連亙數里。

manualTranslations.literal: First month of Jingfu 1, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou, relying on Yan aid, led more than one hundred thousand men to attack Yaoshan in Xingzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jingfu 1, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou, backed by the Yan, marched more than one hundred thousand men against Yaoshan in Xingzhou.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wuhuang sent Li Cunxin to relieve the siege, but Li Cunxiao, long at odds with Cunxin, each suspecting the other, kept his troops from advancing.

manualTranslations.zh: 武皇又遣李嗣勳、李存審將兵援之，大破燕、趙之眾，斬首三萬，收其軍實。
manualTranslations.literal: Wuhuang also sent Li Sixin and Li Cunshen with troops to reinforce them, thoroughly defeated the Yan and Zhao forces, beheaded thirty thousand, and seized their military stores.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wuhuang then sent Li Sixin and Li Cunshen to reinforce them, routed the Yan and Zhao armies, took thirty thousand heads, and captured their stores.

manualTranslations.zh: 三月，武皇進軍渡滹沱，攻欒城，下鼓城、槁城。
manualTranslations.literal: Third month, Wuhuang advanced, crossed the Hutuo, attacked Luancheng, and took Gucheng and Gaocheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month he advanced across the Hutuo, attacked Luancheng, and took Gucheng and Gaocheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 四月，燕軍寇雲、代，武皇班師。
manualTranslations.literal: Fourth month, Yan troops raided Yun and Dai; Wuhuang withdrew the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Yan forces raided Yun and Dai, and Wuhuang withdrew.

sourceRange.text: 天復元年正月，汴將張存敬攻陷晉、絳二州，以兵二萬屯絳州，以扼援路。二月，張存敬迫河中，王珂告急於武皇，使者相望於路。邠國夫人，武皇愛女也，亦以書至，懇切求援。武皇報曰：「賊阻道路，眾寡不敵，救爾即與爾兩亡，可與王郎棄城歸朝。」珂遂送款於張存敬。三月，汴帥自大梁至河中，王珂遂出迎，尋徙於汴。天子以汴帥兼鎮河中，武皇自是不復能援京師，霸業由是中否。

manualTranslations.zh: 天復元年正月，汴將張存敬攻陷晉、絳二州，以兵二萬屯絳州，以扼援路。
manualTranslations.literal: First month of Tianfu 1, Bian general Zhang Cunjing captured Jin and Jiang prefectures and garrisoned Jiang with twenty thousand men to block relief routes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianfu 1, Zhang Cunjing of Bian took Jin and Jiang prefectures and posted twenty thousand men at Jiang to cut off relief.

manualTranslations.zh: 二月，張存敬迫河中，王珂告急於武皇，使者相望於路。
manualTranslations.literal: Second month, Zhang Cunjing pressed Heyang; Wang Ke urgently appealed to Wuhuang, and envoys crowded the road.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month Zhang Cunjing pressed Heyang; Wang Ke begged Wuhuang for aid, and envoys crowded the road.

manualTranslations.zh: 邠國夫人，武皇愛女也，亦以書至，懇切求援。
manualTranslations.literal: The Lady of Bin—Wuhuang's beloved daughter—also sent a letter, pleading urgently for aid.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Lady of Bin, Wuhuang's beloved daughter, also wrote, pleading urgently for help.

manualTranslations.zh: 武皇報曰：「賊阻道路，眾寡不敵，救爾即與爾兩亡，可與王郎棄城歸朝。」
manualTranslations.literal: Wuhuang replied: "Bandits block the roads; numbers are unequal. Saving you would destroy us both—you and Lord Wang should abandon the city and return to court."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wuhuang answered, "The bandits block the roads and we are outnumbered. Saving you would destroy us both—you and Lord Wang should abandon the city and submit to court."

manualTranslations.zh: 珂遂送款於張存敬。
manualTranslations.literal: Ke then submitted allegiance to Zhang Cunjing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ke then surrendered to Zhang Cunjing.

manualTranslations.zh: 三月，汴帥自大梁至河中，王珂遂出迎，尋徙於汴。
manualTranslations.literal: Third month, the Bian commander came from Daliang to Heyang; Wang Ke went out to welcome him and was soon moved to Bian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month the Bian commander came from Daliang to Heyang; Wang Ke went out to welcome him and was soon transferred to Bian.

manualTranslations.zh: 天子以汴帥兼鎮河中，武皇自是不復能援京師，霸業由是中否。
manualTranslations.literal: The Son of Heaven had the Bian commander also command Heyang; Wuhuang could no longer relieve the capital, and his hegemony was thereby checked midway.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor gave the Bian commander joint command of Heyang; Wuhuang could no longer aid the capital, and his bid for hegemony stalled.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingshen Zhou Dewei reported that Chen Que, prefect of Tan, had yielded the city.

sourceRange.text: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝，諱亶，初名嗣源，及即位，改今諱，代北人也。世事武皇，及其錫姓也，遂編於屬籍。四代祖諱聿，皇贈麟州刺史。天成初，追尊為孝恭皇帝，廟號惠祖，陵曰遂陵；高祖妣衛國夫人崔氏，追諡為孝恭昭皇后。三代祖諱教，皇贈朔州刺史，追尊為孝質皇帝，廟號毅祖，陵曰衍陵；曾祖妣趙國夫人張氏，追諡為孝質順皇后。皇祖諱琰，皇贈尉州刺史，追尊為孝靖皇帝，廟號烈祖，陵曰奕陵；皇祖妣秦國夫人何氏，追諡為孝靖穆皇后。皇考諱霓，皇贈汾州刺史，追尊為孝成皇帝，廟號德祖，陵曰慶陵；皇妣宋國夫人劉氏，追諡為孝成懿皇后。帝即孝成之元子也。以唐咸通丁亥歲九月九日，懿皇后生帝於應州之金城縣。

context.afterSource: 初，孝成事唐獻祖為愛將，獻祖之失振武，為吐渾所攻，部下離散，孝成獨奮忠義，解蔚州之圍。

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝，諱亶，初名嗣源，及即位，改今諱，代北人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Mingzong, Emperor of Sagely Virtue, Harmonious Martiality, and Reverent Filial Piety, bore the taboo name Dan; his original name was Siyuan; upon taking the throne he changed to his present taboo name; he was a native of northern Dai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingzong, the Sagely, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverent Filial Emperor, was named Dan; originally Siyuan, he changed to his present taboo name at accession; he came from northern Dai.

manualTranslations.zh: 世事武皇，及其錫姓也，遂編於屬籍。
manualTranslations.literal: In life he served Wuhuang, and when the surname was granted he was enrolled in the clan registers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He served Wuhuang in life, and when the surname was granted he was entered in the clan registers.

manualTranslations.zh: 四代祖諱聿，皇贈麟州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor bore the taboo name Yu and was posthumously granted governor of Lin prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His fourth-generation ancestor Yu was posthumously made governor of Lin.

manualTranslations.zh: 天成初，追尊為孝恭皇帝，廟號惠祖，陵曰遂陵；
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaogong, with temple name Huizu and mausoleum called Suiling;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In early Tiancheng he was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaogong, temple name Huizu, with tomb Suiling;

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖妣衛國夫人崔氏，追諡為孝恭昭皇后。
manualTranslations.literal: His great-great-grandmother, Lady Cui of the State of Wei, was posthumously given the temple name Empress Xiaogong Zhao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Great-great-grandmother Lady Cui of Wei was posthumously styled Empress Xiaogong Zhao.

manualTranslations.zh: 三代祖諱教，皇贈朔州刺史，追尊為孝質皇帝，廟號毅祖，陵曰衍陵；
manualTranslations.literal: His third-generation ancestor bore the taboo name Jiao, was posthumously granted governor of Shuo prefecture, posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaozhi, with temple name Yizu and mausoleum called Yanling;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Third-generation ancestor Jiao was posthumously made Shuo governor and honored as Emperor Xiaozhi, temple name Yizu, tomb Yanling;

manualTranslations.zh: 曾祖妣趙國夫人張氏，追諡為孝質順皇后。
manualTranslations.literal: His great-grandmother, Lady Zhang of the State of Zhao, was posthumously given the temple name Empress Xiaozhi Shun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Great-grandmother Lady Zhang of Zhao was posthumously styled Empress Xiaozhi Shun.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇祖諱琰，皇贈尉州刺史，追尊為孝靖皇帝，廟號烈祖，陵曰奕陵；
manualTranslations.literal: His imperial grandfather bore the taboo name Yan, was posthumously granted governor of Yu prefecture, posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaojing, with temple name Liezu and mausoleum called Yiling;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Imperial grandfather Yan was posthumously made Yu governor and honored as Emperor Xiaojing, temple name Liezu, tomb Yiling;

manualTranslations.zh: 皇祖妣秦國夫人何氏，追諡為孝靖穆皇后。
manualTranslations.literal: His imperial grandmother, Lady He of the State of Qin, was posthumously given the temple name Empress Xiaojing Mu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Imperial grandmother Lady He of Qin was posthumously styled Empress Xiaojing Mu.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇考諱霓，皇贈汾州刺史，追尊為孝成皇帝，廟號德祖，陵曰慶陵；
manualTranslations.literal: His imperial father bore the taboo name Ni, was posthumously granted governor of Fen prefecture, posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaocheng, with temple name Dezu and mausoleum called Qingling;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Imperial father Ni was posthumously made Fen governor and honored as Emperor Xiaocheng, temple name Dezu, tomb Qingling;

manualTranslations.zh: 皇妣宋國夫人劉氏，追諡為孝成懿皇后。
manualTranslations.literal: His imperial mother, Lady Liu of the State of Song, was posthumously given the temple name Empress Xiaocheng Yi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Imperial mother Lady Liu of Song was posthumously styled Empress Xiaocheng Yi.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝即孝成之元子也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor was the eldest son of Xiaocheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Emperor was Xiaocheng's eldest son.

manualTranslations.zh: 以唐咸通丁亥歲九月九日，懿皇后生帝於應州之金城縣。
manualTranslations.literal: In the dinghai year of Tang Xiantong, on the ninth day of the ninth month, Empress Yi gave birth to the Emperor in Jincheng county of Ying prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the dinghai year of Xiantong, on the ninth day of the ninth month, Empress Yi bore him in Jincheng in Ying.

manualTranslations.zh: 天成四年春正月壬申朔，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如儀。
manualTranslations.literal: In spring, first month of Tiancheng 4, on the renshen new moon the Emperor held audience at the Chongyuan Hall and received congratulations; guards and escort followed the usual rite.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the renshen new moon of the first month of Tiancheng 4 Mingzong received New Year congratulations at the Chongyuan Hall with the usual guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 幽州節度使趙德鈞奏：「臣孫讚，年五歲，默念《論語》、《孝經》，舉童子，於汴州取解就試。」
manualTranslations.literal: Youzhou military commissioner Zhao Dejun memorialized: "Your servant's grandson Zan, five years old, recites from memory the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety, passed the child-candidate examination, and begs leave to take qualifying examinations at Bian."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Dejun of Youzhou reported his five-year-old grandson Zan, who memorized the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety as a child candidate and sought to sit the qualifying exams at Bian.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔曰：「都尉之子，太尉之孫，能念儒書，備彰家訓，不勞就試，特與成名。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict said: "Son of a commandant and grandson of a grand commandant, able to recite Confucian classics and clearly manifest family teaching, need not sit the examination—special passing is granted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court replied: "As son of a commandant and grandson of a grand commandant, reciting Confucian classics and showing family teaching, he need not sit the exam—

manualTranslations.zh: 宜賜別敕及第，附今年春榜。」
manualTranslations.literal: A special edict and passing grade are fitting, attached to this year's spring list."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: grant a special patent and passing status, attached to this spring's list."

manualTranslations.zh: 戊子，放元年應欠秋稅。
manualTranslations.literal: On wuzi, unpaid autumn taxes due from the inaugural year were remitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On wuzi unpaid autumn taxes owed from the inaugural year were remitted.

manualTranslations.zh: 以左衛上將軍安崇阮為黔南節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: Left Guard senior general An Chongruan was made Qiannan military commissioner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Left Guard senior general An Chongruan became Qiannan commissioner.

manualTranslations.zh: 壬辰，回鶻入朝使掣撥等五人各授懷化司戈放還。
manualTranslations.literal: On renchen, Huihu court envoy Chebo and five others were each appointed Huaihua Company Commanders and sent home.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renchen Huihu court envoy Chebo and five others were each made Huaihua Company Commanders and sent home.

manualTranslations.zh: 以北京副留守馮贇為宣徽使、判三司。
manualTranslations.literal: Beijing deputy regent Feng Yun was made Palace Treasury Commissioner and overseer of the Revenue Commission.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Beijing deputy regent Feng Yun became palace treasury commissioner and revenue overseer.

manualTranslations.zh: 戊戌，禁天下虛稱試攝銜。
manualTranslations.literal: On wuxu, false use throughout the realm of provisional appointment titles was forbidden.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On wuxu false use of provisional appointment titles was forbidden throughout the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 西川孟知祥奏：「支屬刺史乞臣本道自署。」
manualTranslations.literal: Meng Zhixiang of Western Shu memorialized: "I beg that branch prefects be appointed by this circuit itself."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang of Western Shu asked that branch prefects be appointed by his circuit itself.

sourceRange.text: 長興元年春正月丙寅朔，帝御明堂殿受朝賀，仗衛如常儀。乙亥，國子監請以監學生束修及光學錢備監中修葺公用，從之。丙子，帝謂宰臣曰：「時雪未降，如何？」馮道曰：「陛下恭行儉德，憂及蒸民，上合天心，必有春澤。」是夜，降雪。其夕，右散騎常侍蕭希甫封狀申樞密稱，得河堰衙官狀，告本都將校二十餘人欲謀不軌，至旦追問無狀，斬所告人。是日，幸至德宮。辛卯，中書奏，郊天有日，合差大內留守。詔以宣徽南院使朱宏昭充。

context.afterSource: 二月戊戌，幸稻田莊。
context.afterLocal: 二月戊戌，幸稻田莊。

manualTranslations.zh: 長興元年春正月丙寅朔，帝御明堂殿受朝賀，仗衛如常儀。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Changxing, spring, first month, bingyin new moon: the Emperor took the Bright Hall to receive court congratulations; guards and retinue were as usual.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the bingyin new moon of the first month in spring of Changxing 1 Mingzong received New Year congratulations at the Bright Hall with the usual ceremonial guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 乙亥，國子監請以監學生束修及光學錢備監中修葺公用，從之。
manualTranslations.literal: On yihai the Directorate of Education requested that supervisory students' presentation gifts and optics fees be used for repairs and public expenses within the directorate. It was approved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On yihai the Imperial Academy asked to use student presentation fees and optics funds for institute repairs. Approved.

manualTranslations.zh: 丙子，帝謂宰臣曰：「時雪未降，如何？」
manualTranslations.literal: On bingzi the Emperor said to the chancellors: "Snow has not yet fallen—what of it?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingzi Mingzong asked the chancellors: "Snow has not yet fallen—what of it?"

manualTranslations.zh: 馮道曰：「陛下恭行儉德，憂及蒸民，上合天心，必有春澤。」
manualTranslations.literal: Feng Dao said: "Your Majesty practices frugal virtue and cares for the common people—this accords with Heaven's heart; spring moisture will surely come."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said: "Your Majesty practices frugal virtue and cares for the people—that accords with Heaven, and spring rains will surely come."

manualTranslations.zh: 是夜，降雪。
manualTranslations.literal: That night snow fell.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That night snow fell.

manualTranslations.zh: 其夕，右散騎常侍蕭希甫封狀申樞密稱，得河堰衙官狀，告本都將校二十餘人欲謀不軌，至旦追問無狀，斬所告人。
manualTranslations.literal: That evening Right Regular Cavalier Xiao Xifu submitted a sealed memorial to the Military Secretariat reporting that he had received a petition from a river-dike yamen officer accusing more than twenty local commanders and officers of plotting sedition; by dawn interrogation found no evidence, and the accuser was executed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That evening right regular cavalier Xiao Xifu sent a sealed report to the military secretariat saying a river-dike yamen officer had accused more than twenty local officers of plotting rebellion; by dawn no evidence was found and the accuser was executed.

manualTranslations.zh: 是日，幸至德宮。
manualTranslations.literal: That day he visited the Palace of Utmost Virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That day Mingzong visited the Palace of Utmost Virtue.

manualTranslations.zh: 辛卯，中書奏，郊天有日，合差大內留守。
manualTranslations.literal: On xinmao the Secretariat memorialized that the suburban sacrifice to Heaven had a set date and a Grand Inner Custodian should be appointed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On xinmao the secretariat reported that the suburban sacrifice to Heaven had been scheduled and a grand inner custodian should be appointed.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔以宣徽南院使朱宏昭充。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict appointed Zhu Hongzhao, commissioner of the southern bureau of the Palace Secretariat, to the post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhao, palace secretariat southern commissioner, was appointed to fill the post.

sourceRange.text: 九月壬午，以鎮南軍節度使、檢校太尉馬希範為湖南節度使、檢校太尉、兼侍中。甲申，荊南節度使、檢校太傅、兼中書令高從誨加檢校太尉、兼中書令。壬辰，供奉官李瑰自西川回，節度使孟知祥附表陳敘隔絕之由，並進物，先賜金器等。瑰，知祥甥也，母在蜀，故今瑰往焉。瑰至蜀，具述朝廷厚待之意，知祥稱藩如初，奏福慶長公主以今年正月十二日薨。又奏五月三日，大破東川董璋之眾於漢州，收下東川。又表立功將校趙季良等五人，乞授節鉞；部內刺史令錄已下官，乞許墨製補授。帝遣閣門使劉政恩充西川宣諭使。乙巳，契丹遣使自幽州進馬。秦州地震。

manualTranslations.literal: On renwu in the ninth month, Ma Xifan, military commissioner of the Zhennan army and Grand Guardian ad honorem, was made Hunan military commissioner, Grand Guardian ad honorem, and concurrently vice director.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renwu in the ninth month Ma Xifan, Zhennan army commissioner and Grand Guardian ad honorem, was made Hunan commissioner, Grand Guardian ad honorem, and concurrent vice director.

manualTranslations.zh: 甲申，荊南節度使、檢校太傅、兼中書令高從誨加檢校太尉、兼中書令。
manualTranslations.literal: On jiashen, Gao Conghui, Jingnan military commissioner, Grand Tutor ad honorem, and concurrent secretariat director, was further made Grand Guardian ad honorem and concurrent secretariat director.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiashen Gao Conghui, Jingnan commissioner and concurrent secretariat director, was further made Grand Guardian ad honorem and concurrent secretariat director.

manualTranslations.zh: 壬辰，供奉官李瑰自西川回，節度使孟知祥附表陳敘隔絕之由，並進物，先賜金器等。
manualTranslations.literal: On renchen, attendant envoy Li Gui returned from western Sichuan; military commissioner Meng Zhixiang attached a memorial explaining the reasons for estrangement and also presented goods; gold vessels and such were bestowed first.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renchen Li Gui returned from western Sichuan; Meng Zhixiang attached a memorial on the estrangement and presented goods, and gold vessels were bestowed first.

manualTranslations.zh: 瑰，知祥甥也，母在蜀，故今瑰往焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Gui was Zhixiang's nephew; his mother was in Shu, so Gui had now been sent there.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gui was Zhixiang's nephew; his mother was in Shu, so Gui had been sent there.

manualTranslations.zh: 瑰至蜀，具述朝廷厚待之意，知祥稱藩如初，奏福慶長公主以今年正月十二日薨。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gui reached Shu he fully conveyed the court's generous treatment; Zhixiang declared himself a vassal as before and memorialized that Princess of Blessing and Celebration had died on the twelfth day of the first month this year.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Shu Gui conveyed the court's generous treatment; Zhixiang declared vassalage as before and reported that Princess of Blessing and Celebration had died on the twelfth of the first month this year.

manualTranslations.zh: 又奏五月三日，大破東川董璋之眾於漢州，收下東川。
manualTranslations.literal: He also memorialized that on the third day of the fifth month he had utterly defeated Dong Zhang of eastern Sichuan's forces at Hanzhou and taken eastern Sichuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also reported that on the third of the fifth month he had routed Dong Zhang of eastern Sichuan at Hanzhou and taken eastern Sichuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 又表立功將校趙季良等五人，乞授節鉞；
manualTranslations.literal: He also petitioned that Zhao Jiliang and four other meritorious officers and commandants be granted military commissioner seals;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also asked military commissioner seals for Zhao Jiliang and four other meritorious officers;

manualTranslations.zh: 部內刺史令錄已下官，乞許墨製補授。
manualTranslations.literal: for prefects, magistrates, recorders, and officials below within his jurisdiction he asked permission to appoint by provisional ink edict.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and asked permission to appoint prefects, magistrates, recorders, and lower officials within his jurisdiction by provisional ink edict.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝遣閣門使劉政恩充西川宣諭使。
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor dispatched gate commissioner Liu Zheng'en to serve as western Sichuan edict-announcing commissioner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent gate commissioner Liu Zheng'en as western Sichuan edict-announcing commissioner.

manualTranslations.zh: 乙巳，契丹遣使自幽州進馬。
manualTranslations.literal: On yisi the Khitan sent envoys from Youzhou presenting horses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On yisi Khitan envoys from Youzhou presented horses.

manualTranslations.zh: 秦州地震。
manualTranslations.literal: Qinzhou had an earthquake.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qinzhou had an earthquake.

sourceRange.text: 天成元年，授金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒。二年四月，加檢校太保、同平章事、河南尹，判六軍諸衛事。十一月，加檢校太傅。三年三月，授汴州節度使。四年，移鎮河東。長興元年，改授鎮州節度使，尋封宋王。二年，加檢校太尉、兼侍中，移鎮鄴都。三年，加中書令。秦王從榮，帝同母兄也，以帝有德望，深所猜忌。帝在鄴宮，憂其禍，然善於承順，竟免閑隙。

context.beforeSource: 帝髫齔好讀《春秋》，略通大義，貌類明宗，尤鍾愛。
context.afterSource: 四年十一月二十日，秦王誅。
context.beforeLocal: 帝髫齔好讀《春秋》，略通大義，貌類明宗，尤鍾愛。
context.afterLocal: 四年十一月二十日，秦王誅。

manualTranslations.zh: 天成元年，授金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed Grand Master of the Gold Purple and Radiant Tally and honorary Minister of Works.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng he was made Grand Master of the Gold Purple and Radiant Tally and honorary Minister of Works.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年四月，加檢校太保、同平章事、河南尹，判六軍諸衛事。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year he was advanced honorary Grand Guardian, co-equal Grand Counsellor, and Mayor of Henan, and was empowered over the Six Armies and various guards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year he was advanced honorary Grand Guardian, made co-equal Grand Counsellor and mayor of Henan, and given charge of the Six Armies and palace guards.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一月，加檢校太傅。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh month he was advanced honorary Grand Mentor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was advanced honorary Grand Mentor.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年三月，授汴州節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month of the third year he was appointed Bianzhou military commissioner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year he was made commissioner of Bianzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年，移鎮河東。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year he transferred his command to Hedong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he transferred his command to Hedong.

manualTranslations.zh: 長興元年，改授鎮州節度使，尋封宋王。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Changxing he was reassigned as Zhenzhou military commissioner and soon enfeoffed Prince of Song.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changxing he was reassigned as commissioner of Zhenzhou and soon enfeoffed Prince of Song.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年，加檢校太尉、兼侍中，移鎮鄴都。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year he was advanced honorary Grand Commandant and concurrent Palace Attendant and transferred his command to Yedu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second year he was advanced honorary Grand Commandant and concurrent Palace Attendant and transferred his command to Yedu.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，加中書令。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year he was advanced Director of the Secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Director of the Secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 秦王從榮，帝同母兄也，以帝有德望，深所猜忌。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince of Qin Congrong was the Emperor's elder brother by the same mother; because the Emperor had virtue and prestige, he was deeply suspected and resented.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin Congrong was the Emperor's elder brother by the same mother. Because the Emperor enjoyed virtue and prestige, Congrong deeply suspected and resented him.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝在鄴宮，憂其禍，然善於承順，竟免閑隙。
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor was at the palace in Ye, fearing harm from him, yet was skilled at compliance and deference and ultimately avoided open estrangement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Emperor at the palace in Ye feared harm from him, yet was skilled at compliance and deference and ultimately avoided open estrangement.

sourceRange.text: 應順元年春正月壬申朔，帝御廣壽殿視朝，百僚詣閣門奉慰。時議者雲，月首以朝服臨，不視朝可也。乙亥，契丹遣使朝貢。（《遼史·太宗紀》：天顯九年閏月戊午，唐遣使來告哀，即日遣使祭吊。）丁丑，以太常卿崔居儉為秘書監，以前蔡州刺史張繼祚為左武衛上將軍，充山陵橋道頓遞副使。戊寅，禦明堂殿，仗衛如儀，宮懸樂作，群臣朝服就位，宣製大赦天下，改長興五年為應順元年。時議者以梓宮在殯，宮縣樂作，非禮也，懸而不作可也。回鶻可汗仁美遣使貢方物，故可汗仁裕進遺留馬。是日，命中使三十五人以先帝鞍馬衣帶分賜藩位。

context.beforeSource: 」命徹之。
context.afterSource: 庚辰，宰臣馮道加司空，李愚加右僕射，劉煦加吏部尚書，餘並如故。
context.beforeLocal: 命徹之。
context.afterLocal: 庚辰，宰臣馮道加司空，李愚加右僕射，劉煦加吏部尚書，餘並如故。

manualTranslations.zh: 應順元年春正月壬申朔，帝御廣壽殿視朝，百僚詣閣門奉慰。
manualTranslations.literal: In spring, first month of the first year of Yingshun, on the renshen new moon the Emperor took the Hall of Broad Longevity to hold court; the hundred officials went to the Gate of the Chancellery to offer condolences.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the renshen new moon of the first month of spring in the first year of Yingshun the Emperor held court in the Hall of Broad Longevity, and the hundred officials went to the Gate of the Chancellery to offer condolences.

manualTranslations.zh: 時議者雲，月首以朝服臨，不視朝可也。
manualTranslations.literal: Commentators at the time said that at the month's beginning, to appear in court dress without holding court would suffice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Commentators at the time said that at the month's beginning it would suffice to appear in court dress without holding full court.

manualTranslations.zh: 乙亥，契丹遣使朝貢。
manualTranslations.literal: On yihai the Khitan sent envoys with tribute.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On yihai the Khitan sent envoys with tribute.

manualTranslations.zh: （《遼史·太宗紀》：天顯九年閏月戊午，唐遣使來告哀，即日遣使祭吊。）
manualTranslations.literal: (The Basic Annals of Emperor Taizong in the History of Liao: In the intercalary month of the ninth year of Tianxian, on wuwu, Tang sent envoys to announce mourning, and that same day envoys were sent to offer sacrifices and condolences.)
manualTranslations.idiomatic: (The Basic Annals of Emperor Taizong in the History of Liao records that in the intercalary month of Tianxian 9, on wuwu, Tang sent envoys to announce mourning, and that same day envoys were dispatched to offer sacrifices and condolences.)

manualTranslations.zh: 丁丑，以太常卿崔居儉為秘書監，以前蔡州刺史張繼祚為左武衛上將軍，充山陵橋道頓遞副使。
manualTranslations.literal: On dingchou Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Jujian was made Director of the Secretariat; former Cai Prefecture prefect Zhang Jizuo was made General of the Left Martial Guard and appointed deputy commissioner for imperial tomb bridges, roads, and relay stations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingchou Cui Jujian, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Director of the Secretariat; Zhang Jizuo, former prefect of Cai, was made General of the Left Martial Guard and appointed deputy commissioner for imperial tomb bridges, roads, and relay stations.

manualTranslations.zh: 戊寅，禦明堂殿，仗衛如儀，宮懸樂作，群臣朝服就位，宣製大赦天下，改長興五年為應順元年。
manualTranslations.literal: On wuyin he took the Hall of the Bright Hall; guards and escort followed the rite, palace suspended music was played, the ministers took their places in court dress, and an edict proclaimed a general amnesty for all under heaven, changing the fifth year of Changxing to the first year of Yingshun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On wuyin he took the Hall of the Bright Hall with guards and escort as prescribed, palace music was played, and the ministers in court dress took their places. An edict proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the fifth year of Changxing to the first year of Yingshun.

manualTranslations.zh: 時議者以梓宮在殯，宮縣樂作，非禮也，懸而不作可也。
manualTranslations.literal: Commentators at the time held that with the imperial coffin still in mourning, to play suspended palace music was contrary to ritual; to hang the instruments without playing them would suffice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Commentators held that with the imperial coffin still in mourning, playing suspended palace music was contrary to ritual and that hanging the instruments without playing them would suffice.

manualTranslations.zh: 回鶻可汗仁美遣使貢方物，故可汗仁裕進遺留馬。
manualTranslations.literal: The Uyghur khan Renmei sent envoys with local products; the former khan Renyu presented horses left behind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Uyghur khan Renmei sent envoys with local products, and former khan Renyu presented horses left behind.

manualTranslations.zh: 是日，命中使三十五人以先帝鞍馬衣帶分賜藩位。
manualTranslations.literal: That day thirty-five inner envoys were ordered to distribute the late emperor's saddles, horses, garments, and belts among the frontier lords.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That day thirty-five inner envoys were ordered to distribute the late emperor's saddles, horses, garments, and belts among the frontier lords.

sourceRange.text: 母昭懿皇后夏氏，以歲在甲戌，十一月二十八日庚申，生帝於晉陽舊第。

localRange.text: 母昭懿皇后夏氏，以天祐十一年歲在甲戌，十一月二十八日庚申，生帝於晉陽舊第。

context.beforeSource: 閔帝，諱從厚，小字菩薩奴，明宗第三子也。
context.afterSource: 帝髫齔好讀《春秋》，略通大義，貌類明宗，尤鍾愛。

sourceRange.text: 四月三日，潞王入洛。五日，即位。七日，廢帝為鄂王。遣弘贄子殿直王巒之衛州，時宏贄已奉帝幸州廨。九日，巒至，帝遇鴆而崩，時年二十一。是日辰時，白虹貫日。皇后孔氏在宮中，及王巒回，即日與其四子並遇害。晉高祖即位，諡曰閔，與秦王及末帝子重吉並葬於徽陵域中，封才數尺，路人觀者悲之。

context.beforeSource: 是日，敬瑭盡誅帝之從騎五十餘輩，獨留帝於驛，乃馳騎趨洛。
context.afterSource: 史臣曰：閔帝爰自衝年，素有令問，及征從代邸，入踐堯階，屬軒皇之弓劍初遺，吳王之几杖未賜，遽生猜間，遂至奔亡。
context.beforeLocal: 是日，敬瑭盡誅帝之從騎五十餘輩，獨留帝於驛，乃馳騎趨洛。
context.afterLocal: 史臣曰：閔帝爰自衝年，素有令問，及征從代邸，入踐堯階，屬軒皇之弓劍初遺，吳王之几杖未賜，遽生猜間，遂至奔亡。

manualTranslations.zh: 四月三日，潞王入洛。
manualTranslations.literal: On the third day of the fourth month the Prince of Lu entered Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the third day of the fourth month the Prince of Lu entered Luoyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 五日，即位。
manualTranslations.literal: On the fifth day he took the throne.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the fifth day he took the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 七日，廢帝為鄂王。
manualTranslations.literal: On the seventh day the Emperor was demoted to Prince of E.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the seventh day the Emperor was demoted to Prince of E.

manualTranslations.zh: 遣弘贄子殿直王巒之衛州，時宏贄已奉帝幸州廨。
manualTranslations.literal: He dispatched Hongzan's son, Palace Guard Wang Luan, to Weizhou; by then Hongzan had already escorted the Emperor to the prefectural offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He dispatched Hongzan's son, Palace Guard Wang Luan, to Weizhou; by then Hongzan had already escorted the Emperor to the prefectural offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 九日，巒至，帝遇鴆而崩，時年二十一。
manualTranslations.literal: On the ninth day Luan arrived; the Emperor met poisoned wine and died, aged twenty-one.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the ninth day Luan arrived; the Emperor was given poisoned wine and died, aged twenty-one.

manualTranslations.zh: 是日辰時，白虹貫日。
manualTranslations.literal: That day at the chen hour a white rainbow pierced the sun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That day at the chen hour a white rainbow pierced the sun.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇后孔氏在宮中，及王巒回，即日與其四子並遇害。
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Kong was in the palace; when Wang Luan returned, that same day she and her four sons were all killed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Kong was in the palace; when Wang Luan returned, that same day she and her four sons were all killed.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉高祖即位，諡曰閔，與秦王及末帝子重吉並葬於徽陵域中，封才數尺，路人觀者悲之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, he was given the posthumous title Min; he was buried together with the Prince of Qin and the Last Emperor's son Chongji within the precinct of Huiling Mausoleum, the mound only a few feet high, and passersby who saw it were moved to grief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, he was given the posthumous title Min. He was buried together with the Prince of Qin and the Last Emperor's son Chongji within the precinct of Huiling Mausoleum. The mound was only a few feet high, and passersby who saw it were moved to grief.

sourceRange.text: 丙子，詔河南府率京城居民之財以助賞軍。丁丑，又詔預借居民五個月房課，不問士庶，一概施行。帝素輕財好施，自岐下為諸軍推戴，告軍士曰：「候入洛，人賞百千。」至是，以府藏空匱，於是有配率之令，京城庶士自絕者相繼。己卯，衛州奏，此月九日鄂王薨。庚辰，以宰臣劉煦判三司。辛巳，邢州奏，磁州刺史宋令詢自經而卒。令詢，鄂王在藩時都押牙也，故至於是。甲申，帝以鄂王薨，行服於內園，群臣奉慰。癸未，太后、太妃出宮中衣服器用，以助賞軍。乙酉，帝服袞冕禦明堂殿，文武百僚朝服就位，宣製改應順元年為清泰元年，大赦天下，常赦不原者咸赦除之。丁亥，以宣徽北院使郝瓊為宣徽南院使，權判樞密院；以前三司使王玫為宣徽北院使。以隨駕牙將宋審虔為皇城使，劉延朗為莊宅使。鳳翔節度判官韓昭裔為左諫議大夫，充端明殿學士；觀察判官馬裔孫為翰林學士；掌書記李專美為樞密院直學士。戊子，侍衛親軍都指揮使康義誠伏誅。是日，詔曰：樞密使朱宏昭、馮贇、宣徽南院使孟漢瓊、西京留守王思同、前邠州節度使藥彥稠，共相朋煽，妄舉干戈，互興離間之謀，幾構傾亡之禍，宜行顯戮，以快群情，仍削奪官爵雲。

context.beforeSource: 夫如是，則大寶之位，必有冥數，可輕道哉！
context.afterSource: 庚寅，鳳翔奏，西川孟知祥僭稱大蜀，年號明德。
context.beforeLocal: 夫如是，則大寶之位，必有冥數，可輕道哉！
context.afterLocal: 庚寅，鳳翔奏，西川孟知祥僭稱大蜀，年號明德。

manualTranslations.zh: 丙子，詔河南府率京城居民之財以助賞軍。
manualTranslations.literal: On bingzi, an edict ordered Henan Prefecture to levy the property of capital residents to reward the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingzi an edict ordered Henan Prefecture to levy the property of capital residents to reward the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 丁丑，又詔預借居民五個月房課，不問士庶，一概施行。
manualTranslations.literal: On dingchou, another edict ordered advance collection of five months' housing tax from residents, without distinction between gentry and commoners, uniformly enforced.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingchou another edict ordered advance collection of five months' housing tax from residents, without distinction between gentry and commoners, and applied it uniformly.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝素輕財好施，自岐下為諸軍推戴，告軍士曰：「候入洛，人賞百千。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor had always been free with wealth and generous in giving. When the armies at Qi had raised him up, he told the soldiers: "When we enter Luoyang, each man shall receive a reward of one hundred or one thousand."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Emperor had always been free with wealth and generous in giving. When the armies at Qi had raised him up, he told the soldiers, "When we enter Luoyang, each man shall receive a reward of one hundred or one thousand."

manualTranslations.zh: 至是，以府藏空匱，於是有配率之令，京城庶士自絕者相繼。
manualTranslations.literal: Now, because the treasury was empty, there arose orders for apportioned levies, and commoners of the capital who took their own lives followed one after another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now, because the treasury was empty, apportioned levies were ordered, and commoners of the capital who took their own lives followed one after another.

manualTranslations.zh: 己卯，衛州奏，此月九日鄂王薨。
manualTranslations.literal: On jimao, Weizhou reported that on the ninth day of that month the Prince of E had died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jimao Weizhou reported that on the ninth day of that month the Prince of E had died.

manualTranslations.zh: 庚辰，以宰臣劉煦判三司。
manualTranslations.literal: On gengchen, Chief Councillor Liu Xu was assigned to administer the Three Departments.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengchen Chief Councillor Liu Xu was assigned to administer the Three Departments.

manualTranslations.zh: 辛巳，邢州奏，磁州刺史宋令詢自經而卒。
manualTranslations.literal: On xinsi, Xing Prefecture reported that Song Lingxun, prefect of Ci Prefecture, had hanged himself and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On xinsi Xing Prefecture reported that Song Lingxun, prefect of Ci Prefecture, had hanged himself and died.

manualTranslations.zh: 令詢，鄂王在藩時都押牙也，故至於是。
manualTranslations.literal: Lingxun had been the prince's chief military adjutant when the Prince of E was in his fief, and so it came to this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lingxun had been the Prince of E's chief military adjutant when the prince was in his fief, and so it came to this.

manualTranslations.zh: 甲申，帝以鄂王薨，行服於內園，群臣奉慰。
manualTranslations.literal: On jiashen, because the Prince of E had died, the Emperor observed mourning in the inner garden, and the officials came to offer condolences.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiashen, because the Prince of E had died, the Emperor observed mourning in the inner garden and the officials came to offer condolences.

manualTranslations.zh: 癸未，太后、太妃出宮中衣服器用，以助賞軍。
manualTranslations.literal: On guiwei, the Empress Dowager and Imperial Consort brought forth clothing and utensils from the palace to help reward the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guiwei the Empress Dowager and Imperial Consort brought forth clothing and utensils from the palace to help reward the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 乙酉，帝服袞冕禦明堂殿，文武百僚朝服就位，宣製改應順元年為清泰元年，大赦天下，常赦不原者咸赦除之。
manualTranslations.literal: On yiyou, the Emperor donned dark robes and the imperial cap, ascended the Hall of Bright Hall, and the civil and military officials took their places in court dress. An edict was proclaimed changing the first year of Yingshun to the first year of Qingtai, granting a great amnesty throughout the realm; even offenses normally excluded from regular amnesties were entirely pardoned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On yiyou the Emperor donned dark robes and the imperial cap, ascended the Hall of Bright Hall, and the civil and military officials took their places in court dress. An edict was proclaimed changing the first year of Yingshun to the first year of Qingtai, granting a great amnesty throughout the realm; even offenses normally excluded from regular amnesties were entirely pardoned.

manualTranslations.zh: 丁亥，以宣徽北院使郝瓊為宣徽南院使，權判樞密院；
manualTranslations.literal: On dinghai, Hao Qiong, commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Attendants' Service, was made commissioner of the southern bureau and provisionally directed the Bureau of Military Affairs;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dinghai Hao Qiong, commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Attendants' Service, was made commissioner of the southern bureau and provisionally directed the Bureau of Military Affairs;

manualTranslations.zh: 以前三司使王玫為宣徽北院使。
manualTranslations.literal: the former Three Departments commissioner Wang Mei was made commissioner of the northern bureau.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: former Three Departments commissioner Wang Mei was made commissioner of the northern bureau.

manualTranslations.zh: 以隨駕牙將宋審虔為皇城使，劉延朗為莊宅使。
manualTranslations.literal: the escort military adjutant Song Shenqian was made commissioner of the Imperial City, and Liu Yanlang was made commissioner of the palace estates.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: escort military adjutant Song Shenqian was made commissioner of the Imperial City, and Liu Yanlang was made commissioner of the palace estates.

manualTranslations.zh: 鳳翔節度判官韓昭裔為左諫議大夫，充端明殿學士；
manualTranslations.literal: the Fengxiang military governor's aide Han Zhaoyi was made Left Remonstrance and Counsel Grandee and appointed academician of the Hall of Enlightenment;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fengxiang military governor's aide Han Zhaoyi was made Left Remonstrance and Counsel Grandee and appointed academician of the Hall of Enlightenment;

manualTranslations.zh: 觀察判官馬裔孫為翰林學士；
manualTranslations.literal: the surveillance commissioner's aide Ma Yisun was made Hanlin academician;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: surveillance commissioner's aide Ma Yisun was made Hanlin academician;

manualTranslations.zh: 掌書記李專美為樞密院直學士。
manualTranslations.literal: and the chief secretary Li Zhuanmei was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and chief secretary Li Zhuanmei was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 戊子，侍衛親軍都指揮使康義誠伏誅。
manualTranslations.literal: On wuzi, Kang Yicheng, commander of the palace guard's personal army, was executed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On wuzi Kang Yicheng, commander of the palace guard's personal army, was executed.

manualTranslations.zh: 是日，詔曰：樞密使朱宏昭、馮贇、宣徽南院使孟漢瓊、西京留守王思同、前邠州節度使藥彥稠，共相朋煽，妄舉干戈，互興離間之謀，幾構傾亡之禍，宜行顯戮，以快群情，仍削奪官爵雲。
manualTranslations.literal: That day an edict stated: Chief military commissioners Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun, Commissioner of the Southern Bureau Meng Hanqiong, Western Capital garrison commander Wang Sitong, and former Bin Prefecture military governor Yao Yanchou banded together in conspiracy, rashly raised arms, and each stirred schemes of division—nearly bringing about the calamity of national collapse. They should receive open execution to satisfy public sentiment, and their ranks and titles shall be stripped away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That day an edict stated: Chief military commissioners Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun, Commissioner of the Southern Bureau Meng Hanqiong, Western Capital garrison commander Wang Sitong, and former Bin Prefecture military governor Yao Yanchou banded together in conspiracy, rashly raised arms, and each stirred schemes of division—nearly bringing about the calamity of national collapse. They should receive open execution to satisfy public sentiment, and their ranks and titles were to be stripped away.

sourceRange.text: 末帝，諱從珂，本姓王氏，鎮州人也。母宣憲皇后魏氏，以光啟元年歲在乙巳正月二十三日，生帝於平山。景福中，明宗為武皇騎將，略地至平山，遇魏氏，擄之，帝時年十餘歲，明宗養為己子。小字二十三。帝幼謹重寡言，及壯，長七尺餘，方頤大體，材貌雄偉，以驍果稱，明宗甚愛之。在太原，嘗與石敬瑭因擊球同入於趙襄子之廟，見其塑像，屹然起立，帝秘之，私心自負。及從明宗征討，以力戰知名，莊宗嘗曰：「阿三不惟與我同齒，敢戰亦相類。」莊宗與梁軍戰於胡柳陂，兩軍俱撓，帝衛莊宗奪土山，摧驍陣，其軍復振。時明宗先渡河，莊宗不悅，謂明宗曰：「公當為吾死，渡河安往？」明宗待罪，莊宗以帝從戰有功，由是解慍。

context.afterSource: 天祐十八年，莊宗營於河上，議討鎮州。
context.afterLocal: 天祐十八年，莊宗營於河上，議討鎮州。

manualTranslations.zh: 末帝，諱從珂，本姓王氏，鎮州人也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Later Emperor, taboo name Congke, originally surnamed Wang, was a man of Zhen Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Later Emperor, taboo name Congke, originally surnamed Wang, was a native of Zhen Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 母宣憲皇后魏氏，以光啟元年歲在乙巳正月二十三日，生帝於平山。
manualTranslations.literal: His mother was Empress Xuanxian, née Wei. In the first year of Guangqi, in the year yisi, on the twenty-third day of the first month, she gave birth to the Emperor at Pingshan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Xuanxian, née Wei. In the first year of Guangqi, in the yisi year, on the twenty-third day of the first month, she gave birth to the Emperor at Pingshan.

manualTranslations.zh: 景福中，明宗為武皇騎將，略地至平山，遇魏氏，擄之，帝時年十餘歲，明宗養為己子。
manualTranslations.literal: During Jingfu, Mingzong served as a mounted general of the Martial Emperor; while seizing territory he reached Pingshan, encountered Lady Wei, and carried her off. The Emperor was then a little over ten years old, and Mingzong raised him as his own son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Jingfu, Mingzong served as a mounted general under the Martial Emperor. While seizing territory he reached Pingshan, encountered Lady Wei, and carried her off. The Emperor was then a little over ten, and Mingzong raised him as his own son.

manualTranslations.zh: 小字二十三。
manualTranslations.literal: His childhood name was Twenty-Three.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His childhood name was Twenty-Three.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝幼謹重寡言，及壯，長七尺餘，方頤大體，材貌雄偉，以驍果稱，明宗甚愛之。
manualTranslations.literal: As a youth the Emperor was careful, grave, and sparing of speech. When grown, he stood more than seven chi tall, with a broad face and large physique; his talent and appearance were imposing, and he was famed for daring and resolution. Mingzong greatly cherished him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As a youth the Emperor was careful, grave, and sparing of speech. When grown he stood more than seven chi tall, with a broad face and large frame; his talent and bearing were imposing, and he was famed for daring and resolution. Mingzong greatly cherished him.

manualTranslations.zh: 在太原，嘗與石敬瑭因擊球同入於趙襄子之廟，見其塑像，屹然起立，帝秘之，私心自負。
manualTranslations.literal: At Taiyuan, he once entered the shrine of Zhao Xiangzi together with Shi Jingtang while playing ball. They saw its sculpted image rise up stiffly to its feet. The Emperor kept this secret and secretly felt self-assured.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan he once entered the shrine of Zhao Xiangzi with Shi Jingtang while playing ball. They saw its sculpted image rise stiffly to its feet. The Emperor kept this secret and privately took it as a sign of his own destiny.

manualTranslations.zh: 及從明宗征討，以力戰知名，莊宗嘗曰：「阿三不惟與我同齒，敢戰亦相類。」
manualTranslations.literal: When he followed Mingzong on campaigns, he became renowned for fighting fiercely. Zhuangzong once said: "A San is not only of the same age as I; his readiness to fight is likewise similar."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he followed Mingzong on campaign he became renowned for fierce fighting. Zhuangzong once said, "A San is not only my age-mate; his readiness to fight is much the same."

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗與梁軍戰於胡柳陂，兩軍俱撓，帝衛莊宗奪土山，摧驍陣，其軍復振。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuangzong fought the Liang army at Huliupi, both armies faltered. The Emperor guarded Zhuangzong and seized the earthen hill, broke the enemy's fierce ranks, and their army rallied again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong fought the Liang army at Huliupi and both sides faltered, the Emperor guarded Zhuangzong, seized the earthen hill, broke the enemy's elite ranks, and their army rallied again.

manualTranslations.zh: 時明宗先渡河，莊宗不悅，謂明宗曰：「公當為吾死，渡河安往？」
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Mingzong crossed the river first. Zhuangzong was displeased and said to Mingzong: "You ought to die for me—where are you going, crossing the river?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time Mingzong crossed the river first. Zhuangzong was displeased and said to Mingzong, "You ought to die for me—where are you going, crossing the river?"

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗待罪，莊宗以帝從戰有功，由是解慍。
manualTranslations.literal: Mingzong awaited punishment. Because the Emperor had distinguished himself in battle, Zhuangzong thereby set aside his anger.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingzong awaited punishment, but because the Emperor had distinguished himself in battle Zhuangzong set aside his anger.

sourceRange.text: ）明宗昭懿皇后夏氏，生秦王從榮及閔帝。同光初，後以疾崩，明宗即位，追封為晉國夫人。長興中，明宗以秦、宋二王位望既隆，因思從貴之義，乃下製曰：「故晉國夫人夏氏，素推仁德，久睦宗親，嘗施內助之方，不見中興之盛，予當御極，子並為王，有鵲巢之高，無翬衣之貴，貞魂永逝，懿範常存，考本朝之文，沿追冊之制，將慰懷於九族，冀葉慶於四星。宜追冊為皇后，兼定懿號。」既而有司上諡曰昭懿。和武顯皇后曹氏。（案：《曹後傳》，原本闕佚。考《五代會要》云：天成三年正月，冊為淑妃，長興元年五月十四日，冊為皇后；應順元年閏正月，冊為皇太后。至清泰三年閏十一月，隨末帝崩於後樓。晉高祖使人護葬，至天福五年正月二十八日，追冊曰和武顯皇后。

context.beforeSource: 又案《五代會要》：莊宗朝內職，又有昭儀侯氏封汧國夫人，昭媛白氏封沂國夫人，出使美宣鄧氏封珝國夫人，禦正楚真張氏封涼國夫人，司簿德美周氏封宋國夫人，侍真吳氏封延陵郡夫人，懿才王氏封太原郡夫人，鹹一韓氏封昌黎郡夫人，瑤芳張氏封清河郡夫人，懿德王氏封琅琊郡夫人，宣一馬氏封扶風郡夫人，並同光二年十一月敕。
context.afterSource: ）宣憲皇后魏氏。

manualTranslations.zh: ）明宗昭懿皇后夏氏，生秦王從榮及閔帝。
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Zhaoyi Xia of Emperor Mingzong bore the Prince of Qin Congrong and the Min Emperor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaoyi Xia, consort of Mingzong, bore the Prince of Qin Congrong and the Min Emperor.

manualTranslations.zh: 同光初，後以疾崩，明宗即位，追封為晉國夫人。
manualTranslations.literal: In the early Tongguang era the empress died of illness. When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the early Tongguang era she died of illness. When Mingzong took the throne, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 長興中，明宗以秦、宋二王位望既隆，因思從貴之義，乃下製曰：「故晉國夫人夏氏，素推仁德，久睦宗親，嘗施內助之方，不見中興之盛，予當御極，子並為王，有鵲巢之高，無翬衣之貴，貞魂永逝，懿範常存，考本朝之文，沿追冊之制，將慰懷於九族，冀葉慶於四星。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Changxing era, because the rank and prestige of the Princes of Qin and Song had already risen, Emperor Mingzong, reflecting on the principle of honoring one's mother, issued an edict saying, "The late Lady of the State of Jin, Lady Xia, always promoted benevolence and virtue and long kept kin harmonious. She once applied the ways of inner support, yet did not see the splendor of restoration. When I took the throne and my sons were all made princes, she had the height of the magpie's nest yet not the honor of the pheasant robe. Her chaste soul has passed forever, but her excellent example endures. Examining the texts of our dynasty and following the institutions of posthumous enfeoffment, I shall comfort the hearts of the nine clans and hope to bring blessing to the four stars.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Changxing era, as the Princes of Qin and Song had risen in rank and prestige, Mingzong, reflecting on the duty of honoring one's mother, issued an edict: "The late Lady of Jin, Lady Xia, always promoted benevolence and long kept kin harmonious. She aided from within yet did not live to see restoration. When I took the throne and my sons were made princes, she had the magpie's nest yet not the pheasant robe. Her chaste soul has passed, but her excellent example endures. Following our dynasty's texts and the institutions of posthumous enfeoffment, I shall comfort the nine clans and hope to bring blessing to the four stars.

manualTranslations.zh: 宜追冊為皇后，兼定懿號。」
manualTranslations.literal: She should be posthumously enfeoffed as empress, and her excellent honorific title should be fixed."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She should be posthumously enfeoffed as empress, and her excellent honorific title should be fixed."

manualTranslations.zh: 既而有司上諡曰昭懿。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon the responsible offices submitted the posthumous title Zhaoyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The responsible offices thereupon submitted the posthumous title Zhaoyi.

manualTranslations.zh: 和武顯皇后曹氏。
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Hewuxian Cao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Hewuxian Cao.

manualTranslations.zh: （案：《曹後傳》，原本闕佚。
manualTranslations.literal: (Note: The biography of Empress Cao is missing from the original text.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: (Note: The biography of Empress Cao is missing from the original text.

manualTranslations.zh: 考《五代會要》云：天成三年正月，冊為淑妃，長興元年五月十四日，冊為皇后；
manualTranslations.literal: Examining the 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》, it says: In the first month of the third year of Tiancheng she was enfeoffed as pure consort; on the fourteenth day of the fifth month of the first year of Changxing she was enfeoffed as empress;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records that in the first month of Tiancheng 3 she was enfeoffed as pure consort, and on the fourteenth day of the fifth month of Changxing 1 as empress;

manualTranslations.zh: 應順元年閏正月，冊為皇太后。
manualTranslations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the first year of Yingshun she was enfeoffed as empress dowager.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of Yingshun 1 she was enfeoffed as empress dowager.

manualTranslations.zh: 至清泰三年閏十一月，隨末帝崩於後樓。
manualTranslations.literal: By the intercalary eleventh month of the third year of Qingtai she perished with the Last Emperor at the Rear Tower.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month of Qingtai 3 she perished with the Last Emperor at the Rear Tower.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉高祖使人護葬，至天福五年正月二十八日，追冊曰和武顯皇后。
manualTranslations.literal: The Founding Emperor of Jin sent men to escort the burial. On the twenty-eighth day of the first month of the fifth year of Tianfu she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Hewuxian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Jin sent men to escort the burial. On the twenty-eighth day of the first month of Tianfu 5 she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Hewuxian.

sourceRange.text: ）魏國夫人陳氏，襄州人，本昭宗之宮嬪也。乾寧二年，武皇奉詔討王行瑜，駐軍於渭北，昭宗降朱書御劄，出陳氏及內妓四人以賜武皇。陳氏素知書，有才貌，武皇深加寵重。及光化之後，時事多難，武皇常獨居深念，嬪媵鮮得侍謁，唯陳氏得召見。陳氏性既靜退，不以寵侍自侈，武皇常呼為阿者。及武皇大漸之際，陳氏侍醫藥，垂泣言：「妾為王執掃除之役，十有四年矣，王萬一不幸，妾將何托！既不能以身為殉，願落發為尼，為王讀一藏佛經，以報平昔。」武皇為之流涕。及武皇薨，陳氏果落發持經，法名智願，後居於洛陽佛寺，莊宗賜號建法大師。天成中，明帝幸其院，改賜圓惠大師。晉天福中，卒於太原。追諡光國大師，塔以惠寂為名也。

manualTranslations.zh: ）魏國夫人陳氏，襄州人，本昭宗之宮嬪也。
manualTranslations.literal: Lady Chen, Lady of the State of Wei, was a native of Xiang Prefecture and had originally been a palace consort of Emperor Zhaozong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lady Chen, Lady of Wei, was a native of Xiangzhou and had originally been a palace consort of Emperor Zhaozong.

manualTranslations.zh: 乾寧二年，武皇奉詔討王行瑜，駐軍於渭北，昭宗降朱書御劄，出陳氏及內妓四人以賜武皇。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Qianning, the Martial Emperor received orders to campaign against Wang Xingyu and encamped north of the Wei River. Emperor Zhaozong issued an imperial letter in vermilion and sent out Lady Chen and four inner courtesans to bestow upon the Martial Emperor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Qianning 2 Li Keyong received orders to campaign against Wang Xingyu and encamped north of the Wei. Emperor Zhaozong issued an imperial letter in vermilion and sent Lady Chen and four inner courtesans to bestow upon him.

manualTranslations.zh: 陳氏素知書，有才貌，武皇深加寵重。
manualTranslations.literal: Lady Chen was versed in writing and gifted in talent and appearance. The Martial Emperor greatly favored and honored her.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lady Chen was literate and gifted in talent and beauty. Li Keyong greatly favored her.

manualTranslations.zh: 及光化之後，時事多難，武皇常獨居深念，嬪媵鮮得侍謁，唯陳氏得召見。
manualTranslations.literal: After the Guanghua era, the times were full of hardship. The Martial Emperor often sat alone in deep thought; consorts and attendants rarely gained audience, and only Lady Chen was summoned to see him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the Guanghua era, when the times were troubled, Li Keyong often sat alone in deep thought. Consorts and attendants rarely saw him; only Lady Chen was summoned.

manualTranslations.zh: 陳氏性既靜退，不以寵侍自侈，武皇常呼為阿者。
manualTranslations.literal: Lady Chen's nature was calm and retiring, and she did not grow arrogant from favor and attendance. The Martial Emperor often called her A-Zhe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Calm and retiring by nature, Lady Chen did not grow arrogant from favor. Li Keyong often called her A-Zhe.

manualTranslations.zh: 及武皇大漸之際，陳氏侍醫藥，垂泣言：「妾為王執掃除之役，十有四年矣，王萬一不幸，妾將何托！
manualTranslations.literal: As the Martial Emperor drew near his end, Lady Chen attended his medicines and weeping said, "Your servant has performed sweeping and cleaning duties for Your Majesty for fourteen years. If Your Majesty should meet misfortune, whom shall your servant rely upon!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As Li Keyong lay dying, Lady Chen attended his medicines and wept, "I have served you in sweeping and cleaning for fourteen years. If misfortune should befall you, whom shall I rely upon!

manualTranslations.zh: 既不能以身為殉，願落發為尼，為王讀一藏佛經，以報平昔。」
manualTranslations.literal: Since I cannot follow you in death, I wish to shave my head and become a nun, to read one complete Buddhist canon for Your Majesty and repay our former days."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since I cannot die with you, I wish to shave my head and become a nun and read the complete Buddhist canon for you, to repay our former days."

manualTranslations.zh: 武皇為之流涕。
manualTranslations.literal: The Martial Emperor wept for her.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Keyong wept at her words.

manualTranslations.zh: 及武皇薨，陳氏果落發持經，法名智願，後居於洛陽佛寺，莊宗賜號建法大師。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Martial Emperor died, Lady Chen indeed shaved her head and upheld the sutras. Her dharma name was Zhiyuan. Later she resided in a Buddhist monastery in Luoyang, and Emperor Zhuangzong granted her the title Great Master Jianfa.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong died, Lady Chen shaved her head and took up the sutras under the dharma name Zhiyuan. She later lived in a Luoyang monastery, and Zhuangzong granted her the title Great Master Jianfa.

manualTranslations.zh: 天成中，明帝幸其院，改賜圓惠大師。
manualTranslations.literal: During the Tiancheng era, Emperor Ming visited her monastery and changed her grant to Great Master Yuanhui.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era Mingzong visited her monastery and changed her title to Great Master Yuanhui.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉天福中，卒於太原。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin she died at Taiyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She died at Taiyuan during the Jin Tianfu era.

manualTranslations.zh: 追諡光國大師，塔以惠寂為名也。
manualTranslations.literal: She was posthumously honored as Great Master Guangguo, and her pagoda was named Huiji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She was posthumously honored as Great Master Guangguo, and her pagoda was named Huiji.

sourceRange.text: 武皇薨，莊宗嗣晉王位，時李克寧、李存顥謀變，人情危懼。太后召監軍張承業，指莊宗謂之曰：「先人把臂授公此兒，如聞外謀，欲孤付托，公等但置予母子有地，毋令乞食於汴，幸矣。」承業因誅存顥、克寧，以清內難。莊宗善音律，喜伶人謔浪，太后常提耳誨之。天祐七年，鎮、定求援，莊宗促命治兵，太后曰：「予齒漸衰，兒但不墜先人之業為幸矣，何事櫛風沐雨，離我晨昏！」莊宗曰：「稟先王遺旨，須滅仇讎。山東之事，機不可失。」及發，太后餞於汾橋，悲不自勝。莊宗平定趙、魏，駐於鄴城，每一歲之內，馳駕歸寧者數四，民士服其仁孝。太后初封晉國夫人，莊宗即位，命宰臣盧損奉冊書上皇太后尊號。其年平定河南，西幸洛陽，令皇弟存渥、皇子繼岌就太原迎奉。莊宗親至懷州，迎歸長壽宮，太后素與劉太妃善，分訣之後，悒然不樂。俄聞太妃寢疾，尚醫中使，問訊結轍。既而謂莊宗曰：「吾與太妃恩如伯仲，彼經年抱疾，但見吾麵，差足慰心，吾暫至晉陽，旬朔與之俱來。」莊宗曰：「時方暑毒，山路崎嶇，無煩往復，可令存渥輩迎侍太妃。」乃止。及凶問至，太后慟哭累旬，由是不豫，尋崩於長壽宮。同光三年冬十月，上諡曰貞簡皇太后，葬於壽安陵。

context.beforeSource: 及莊宗載誕，體貌奇傑，武皇異而憐之，太后益寵貴，諸夫人鹹出其下，後亦恭勤內助，左右稱之。
context.afterSource: 太妃劉氏，武皇之正室也。

manualTranslations.zh: 武皇薨，莊宗嗣晉王位，時李克寧、李存顥謀變，人情危懼。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Martial Emperor died, Emperor Zhuangzong succeeded to the throne of Prince of Jin. At that time Li Kening and Li Cunhao plotted rebellion, and popular sentiment was alarmed and fearful.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong died, Zhuangzong succeeded as Prince of Jin. Li Kening and Li Cunhao then plotted rebellion, and the court was gripped by fear.

manualTranslations.zh: 太后召監軍張承業，指莊宗謂之曰：「先人把臂授公此兒，如聞外謀，欲孤付托，公等但置予母子有地，毋令乞食於汴，幸矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Empress Dowager summoned the army supervisor Zhang Chengye, pointed to Emperor Zhuangzong, and said to him, "Our forebear clasped your arm and entrusted this child to you. If I hear of outside plots and wish to entrust him alone, you need only secure a place for me and my son—do not let us beg for food at Bian—and that would be fortune enough."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The empress dowager summoned army supervisor Zhang Chengye, pointed to Zhuangzong, and said, "Our forebear clasped your arm and entrusted this boy to you. If outsiders plot and I must rely on you alone, see only that my son and I have somewhere to live and are not reduced to begging at Bian—that will be fortune enough."

manualTranslations.zh: 承業因誅存顥、克寧，以清內難。
manualTranslations.literal: Chengye thereupon executed Cunhao and Kening to settle the internal crisis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chengye executed Cunhao and Kening, clearing the internal threat.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗善音律，喜伶人謔浪，太后常提耳誨之。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong was skilled in music and delighted in the jesting of actors. The Empress Dowager often pulled his ear to admonish him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was skilled in music and loved the coarse jesting of actors. The empress dowager often pulled his ear to warn him.

manualTranslations.zh: 天祐七年，鎮、定求援，莊宗促命治兵，太后曰：「予齒漸衰，兒但不墜先人之業為幸矣，何事櫛風沐雨，離我晨昏！」
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianyou, Zhen and Ding sought aid. Emperor Zhuangzong urgently ordered troops raised. The Empress Dowager said, "My teeth are gradually failing. If my son only does not let our forebears' enterprise fall, that is fortune enough. Why must he brave wind and rain and leave my morning and evening!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 7 Zhen and Ding sought help, and Zhuangzong urgently ordered mobilization. The empress dowager said, "I am growing old. If my son only keeps our forebears' enterprise from falling, that is fortune enough. Why must he brave wind and rain and leave my side morning and evening!"

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗曰：「稟先王遺旨，須滅仇讎。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong said, "Following the late king's final charge, I must destroy our enemy."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "Following my late father's final charge, I must destroy our enemy.

manualTranslations.zh: 山東之事，機不可失。」
manualTranslations.literal: As for affairs in Shandong, the opportunity must not be lost."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for Shandong, the opportunity must not be lost."

manualTranslations.zh: 及發，太后餞於汾橋，悲不自勝。
manualTranslations.literal: When he set out, the Empress Dowager saw him off at Fen Bridge, so grief-stricken she could not contain herself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he set out, the empress dowager saw him off at Fen Bridge, overcome with grief.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗平定趙、魏，駐於鄴城，每一歲之內，馳駕歸寧者數四，民士服其仁孝。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Zhao and Wei and encamped at Ye. Within each year he raced his carriage home to pay respects several times, and the people and officials admired his benevolence and filial piety.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong pacified Zhao and Wei and encamped at Ye, he raced home to pay his respects several times each year, and the people admired his benevolence and filial piety.

manualTranslations.zh: 太后初封晉國夫人，莊宗即位，命宰臣盧損奉冊書上皇太后尊號。
manualTranslations.literal: The Empress Dowager had first been enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Jin. When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, he ordered chief minister Lu Sun to present the patent of enfeoffment and bestow the honored title of empress dowager.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had first been enfeoffed as Lady of Jin. When Zhuangzong took the throne, he ordered chief minister Lu Sun to present the patent and bestow on her the title of empress dowager.

manualTranslations.zh: 其年平定河南，西幸洛陽，令皇弟存渥、皇子繼岌就太原迎奉。
manualTranslations.literal: That year he pacified Henan and traveled west to Luoyang, ordering his younger brother Cunwo and the prince Jiji to go to Taiyuan to escort her.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year he pacified Henan and went west to Luoyang, sending his younger brother Cunwo and Prince Jiji to Taiyuan to escort her.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗親至懷州，迎歸長壽宮，太后素與劉太妃善，分訣之後，悒然不樂。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong personally went as far as Huai Prefecture to welcome her back to Changshou Palace. The Empress Dowager had long been on good terms with Grand Consort Liu; after parting from her, she was depressed and unhappy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong went in person as far as Huaizhou to welcome her to Changshou Palace. The empress dowager had long been close to Grand Consort Liu, and after their parting she was despondent.

manualTranslations.zh: 俄聞太妃寢疾，尚醫中使，問訊結轍。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon word came that the Grand Consort had taken to her bed with illness. Imperial physicians and inner envoys followed one another in inquiries.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon word came that the grand consort had fallen ill. Imperial physicians and inner envoys followed one another with inquiries.

manualTranslations.zh: 既而謂莊宗曰：「吾與太妃恩如伯仲，彼經年抱疾，但見吾麵，差足慰心，吾暫至晉陽，旬朔與之俱來。」
manualTranslations.literal: She then said to Emperor Zhuangzong, "The Grand Consort and I are as close as elder and younger brother. She has been ill for years; if she could only see my face, that would be enough to comfort her heart. I shall go briefly to Jinyang and return with her within a month."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She then told Zhuangzong, "The grand consort and I are as close as sisters. She has been ill for years; seeing my face would comfort her. I shall go briefly to Jinyang and return with her within a month."

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗曰：「時方暑毒，山路崎嶇，無煩往復，可令存渥輩迎侍太妃。」
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong said, "The season is now fiercely hot and poisonous, and the mountain roads are rugged. Do not trouble yourself with the round trip. You may have Cunwo and the others go to attend the Grand Consort."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "The heat is fierce and the mountain roads are rugged. Do not trouble yourself with the journey. Let Cunwo and the others go to attend the grand consort."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃止。
manualTranslations.literal: She thereupon desisted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She desisted.

manualTranslations.zh: 及凶問至，太后慟哭累旬，由是不豫，尋崩於長壽宮。
manualTranslations.literal: When news of the death arrived, the Empress Dowager wailed in grief for many days. Thereafter she was unwell and soon died in Changshou Palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When news of the death arrived, the empress dowager mourned for many days, fell ill, and soon died in Changshou Palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 同光三年冬十月，上諡曰貞簡皇太后，葬於壽安陵。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the third year of Tongguang, she was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Zhenjian and buried at Shou'an Mausoleum.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in Tongguang 3 she was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Zhenjian and buried at Shou'an Mausoleum.

sourceRange.text: 天復元年，河中王珂為汴人所擄，河中晉、絳諸郡皆陷。四月，汾州刺史李瑭謀叛，納款於汴；嗣昭討之，三日而拔，斬瑭。是月，汴人初得蒲、絳，乃大舉諸道之師來逼太原。汴將葛從周陷承天軍，氏叔琮營洞渦驛。太原四面，汴軍雲合，武皇憂迫，計無從出。嗣昭朝夕選精騎分出諸門，掩擊汴營，左俘右斬，或燔或擊，汴軍疲於奔命；又屬霖雨，軍多足腫腹疾，糧運不繼。五月，氏叔琮引退，嗣昭以精騎追之，汴軍委棄輜重兵仗萬計。六月，嗣昭出師陰地，攻慈、隰，降其刺史唐禮、張瑰。是時，天子在鳳翔，汴人攻圍，有密詔征兵。十一月，嗣昭出師晉、絳，屯吉上堡，遇汴將王友通於平陽，一戰擒之。

context.beforeSource: 嗣昭攻其北門，破其外垣，俄而汴將閻寶救軍至，乃退。
context.afterSource: 明年正月，嗣昭進兵蒲縣。
context.beforeLocal: 嗣昭攻其北門，破其外垣，俄而汴將閻寶救軍至，乃退。
context.afterLocal: 明年正月，嗣昭進兵蒲縣。

manualTranslations.zh: 天復元年，河中王珂為汴人所擄，河中晉、絳諸郡皆陷。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Tianfu, Wang Ke of Hezhong was captured by the men of Bian, and all the Jin and Jiang commanderies of Hezhong fell.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 1, Wang Ke of Hezhong was captured by the Bian, and Jin, Jiang, and the other Hezhong commanderies all fell.

manualTranslations.zh: 四月，汾州刺史李瑭謀叛，納款於汴；
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month, Li Tang, prefect of Fen, plotted rebellion and surrendered to Bian;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Li Tang, prefect of Fen, plotted to rebel and offered submission to Bian;

manualTranslations.zh: 嗣昭討之，三日而拔，斬瑭。
manualTranslations.literal: Sizhao attacked him; in three days he took the place and executed Tang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sizhao attacked him, stormed the place within three days, and executed Tang.

manualTranslations.zh: 是月，汴人初得蒲、絳，乃大舉諸道之師來逼太原。
manualTranslations.literal: That month, having newly taken Pu and Jiang, the men of Bian then marshaled armies from all circuits to press Taiyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That same month, with Pu and Jiang newly in their hands, the Bian mustered armies from every circuit to close on Taiyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 汴將葛從周陷承天軍，氏叔琮營洞渦驛。
manualTranslations.literal: The Bian general Ge Congzhou took Chengtian Army, and Shi Shuzong encamped at Dongwo Post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Bian general Ge Congzhou seized Chengtian Army, while Shi Shuzong encamped at Dongwo Post.

manualTranslations.zh: 太原四面，汴軍雲合，武皇憂迫，計無從出。
manualTranslations.literal: On all four sides of Taiyuan the Bian armies gathered like clouds; the Martial Emperor was distressed and pressed, with no plan to be devised.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bian forces massed on every side of Taiyuan. The Martial Emperor was desperate, with no workable plan.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗣昭朝夕選精騎分出諸門，掩擊汴營，左俘右斬，或燔或擊，汴軍疲於奔命；
manualTranslations.literal: Day and night Sizhao selected elite cavalry and sent them out by the various gates to strike Bian camps by surprise, capturing on the left and slaying on the right, sometimes burning and sometimes attacking; the Bian army was worn out from rushing to and fro;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Day and night Sizhao picked elite horsemen and sent them out through every gate to raid Bian camps, seizing prisoners on one flank and cutting down enemies on the other, sometimes setting fires and sometimes striking head-on, until the Bian were exhausted from constant alarms;

manualTranslations.zh: 又屬霖雨，軍多足腫腹疾，糧運不繼。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover it happened to be a season of prolonged rain; many in the army had swollen feet and abdominal ailments, and grain shipments could not keep up.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Prolonged rains added to their woes: many troops suffered swollen feet and bowel illness, and supplies failed to arrive.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月，氏叔琮引退，嗣昭以精騎追之，汴軍委棄輜重兵仗萬計。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month Shi Shuzong withdrew; Sizhao pursued with elite cavalry, and the Bian army abandoned baggage, heavy equipment, and weapons numbering in the tens of thousands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Shi Shuzong pulled back. Sizhao pursued with picked cavalry, and the Bian abandoned tens of thousands of items of baggage, equipment, and arms.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，嗣昭出師陰地，攻慈、隰，降其刺史唐禮、張瑰。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month Sizhao marched from Yindi and attacked Ci and Xi, receiving the surrender of their prefects Tang Li and Zhang Gui.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Sizhao marched from Yindi against Ci and Xi and accepted the surrender of prefects Tang Li and Zhang Gui.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，天子在鳳翔，汴人攻圍，有密詔征兵。
manualTranslations.literal: At this time the Son of Heaven was at Fengxiang, besieged by the men of Bian, and there was a secret edict to raise troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Fengxiang, under siege by the Bian, and a secret edict called for troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一月，嗣昭出師晉、絳，屯吉上堡，遇汴將王友通於平陽，一戰擒之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh month Sizhao marched to Jin and Jiang and encamped at Jishang Fort; at Pingyang he encountered the Bian general Wang Youtong and captured him in a single battle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Sizhao marched into Jin and Jiang and encamped at Jishang Fort. At Pingyang he met the Bian general Wang Youtong and took him in one engagement.

manualTranslations.literal: Dewei was tall with a dark face; when he laughed his expression did not change. Whenever he drew up battle lines against the enemy, he had a stern and awe-inspiring air of killing severity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dewei was tall and dark-faced, and even when he laughed his bearing did not change. On the battlefield he arrayed his lines with a stern, killing severity.

manualTranslations.zh: 中興之朝，號為名將。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Restoration court he was acclaimed as a famous general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the restoration era he was counted among the famous generals.

manualTranslations.zh: 及其歿也，人皆惜之。
manualTranslations.literal: When he died, all men regretted his loss.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he died, everyone mourned the loss.

manualTranslations.zh: 同光初，追贈太師。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tongguang era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

manualTranslations.zh: 天成中，詔與李嗣昭、符存審配饗莊宗廟廷。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he was ordered, with Li Sizhao and Fu Cunshen, to receive collateral offerings in Zhuangzong's temple.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉高祖即位，追封燕王。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozu of Jin took the throne, Dewei was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Yan.

sourceRange.text: 光允，光逢之弟也，（新舊《唐書》俱云：趙隱子三人，光逢、光裔、光允。為後唐相者，光允也。原本作光裔，係誤。）俱以詞藝知名，亦登進士第。（《舊唐書》云：大順二年，進士登第。天祐初，累官至駕部郎中。）光允仕梁，曆清顯，伯仲之間，咸以方雅自高，北人聞其名者，皆望風欽重。及莊宗平定汴、洛，時盧程以狂妄免，郭崇韜自勳臣拜，議者以為國朝典禮故實，須訪前代名家，咸曰光允有宰相器。薛廷珪、李琪當武皇為晉王時，嘗因為冊使至太原，故皆有宿望，當時咸謂宜處台司。郭崇韜采言事者雲，廷珪朽老，浮華無相業；琪雖文學高，傾險無士風，皆不可相，乃止。同光元年十一月，光允與韋說並拜平章事。

context.beforeSource: 詔贈太傅。
