items.sourceTextOverride: 顯德元年正月庚辰，加開府儀同三司、檢校太尉、兼侍中，依前開封尹兼功德使，判內外兵馬事。時太祖寢疾彌留，士庶憂沮，及聞帝總內外兵柄，咸以為愜。〈（《隆平集》：曹翰隸世宗幕下，世宗鎮澶淵，以為牙校。及尹開封，翰猶在澶淵，聞周祖寢疾，不俟召來見世宗，密言曰：「王為冢嗣，不侍醫藥，何以副天下望？」世宗悟，入侍禁中，以府事命翰總決。）〉壬辰，太祖崩，秘不發喪。丙申，內出太祖遺制：「晉王榮可於柩前即位。」群臣奉帝即皇帝位。庚子，宰臣馮道率百僚上表請聽政，凡三上。壬寅，帝見群臣於萬歲殿門之東廡下。

manualTranslations.zh: 顯德元年正月庚辰，加開府儀同三司、檢校太尉、兼侍中，依前開封尹兼功德使，判內外兵馬事。
manualTranslations.literal: On gengchen of the first month of the first year of Xiande, he was granted Grand Minister with the Ceremonial of a Three-Division Commandery, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, and as before remained Mayor of Kaifeng and Merit Commissioner, with charge over internal and external military affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengchen in the first month of the first year of Xiande he was granted Grand Minister with Three-Division ceremonial rank, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, and as before remained mayor of Kaifeng and merit commissioner with authority over all military affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 時太祖寢疾彌留，士庶憂沮，及聞帝總內外兵柄，咸以為愜。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Taizu lay gravely ill and near death; officials and commoners were anxious and downcast, but when they heard that the Emperor had taken overall command of internal and external military power, all felt reassured.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu was then gravely ill and near death, and officials and commoners were anxious; when they heard that the emperor had taken command of all military affairs, they were reassured.

manualTranslations.zh: 〈（《隆平集》：曹翰隸世宗幕下，世宗鎮澶淵，以為牙校。
manualTranslations.literal: (The Longpingji states: Cao Han served under Shizong on his staff; when Shizong was stationed at Chanyuan, Han was made a junior officer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: (According to the Longpingji, Cao Han served on Shizong's staff; when Shizong was stationed at Chanyuan, Han was made a junior officer.

manualTranslations.zh: 及尹開封，翰猶在澶淵，聞周祖寢疾，不俟召來見世宗，密言曰：「王為冢嗣，不侍醫藥，何以副天下望？」
manualTranslations.literal: When Shizong became mayor of Kaifeng, Han was still at Chanyuan; hearing that the Zhou founder lay gravely ill, he came without waiting to be summoned to see Shizong and said privately: "As heir apparent, if you do not attend to medicine and nursing, how can you meet the expectations of the realm?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Shizong became mayor of Kaifeng, Han was still at Chanyuan; hearing that the Zhou founder lay gravely ill, he came unbidden to see Shizong and said privately, "As heir apparent, if you do not attend to medicine and nursing, how can you meet the realm's expectations?"

manualTranslations.zh: 世宗悟，入侍禁中，以府事命翰總決。）〉
manualTranslations.literal: Shizong understood, entered the inner palace to attend him, and entrusted Han with overall authority over prefectural affairs.)〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shizong took the point, entered the inner palace to attend him, and entrusted Han with overall authority over prefectural affairs.)〉

manualTranslations.zh: 壬辰，太祖崩，秘不發喪。
manualTranslations.literal: On renchen Taizu died, and the death was kept secret without announcing mourning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renchen Taizu died; the court kept his death secret and did not yet announce mourning.

manualTranslations.zh: 丙申，內出太祖遺制：「晉王榮可於柩前即位。」
manualTranslations.literal: On bingshen the testamentary order of Taizu was issued from within the palace: "Prince of Jin Rong may take the imperial throne before the coffin."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingshen Taizu's testament was issued from within the palace: "Prince of Jin Rong shall take the throne before the coffin."

manualTranslations.zh: 群臣奉帝即皇帝位。
manualTranslations.literal: The ministers led the Emperor to take the imperial throne.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The ministers led the emperor to take the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 庚子，宰臣馮道率百僚上表請聽政，凡三上。
manualTranslations.literal: On gengzi the chief minister Feng Dao led the hundred officials in submitting a memorial requesting that he attend to government; they submitted three times.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengzi Feng Dao led the full bureaucracy in three memorials asking the new emperor to take up government.

manualTranslations.zh: 壬寅，帝見群臣於萬歲殿門之東廡下。
manualTranslations.literal: On renyin the Emperor received the ministers beneath the eastern corridor of the gate of the Hall of Ten Thousand Years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renyin the emperor received the ministers beneath the eastern corridor at the gate of the Hall of Ten Thousand Years.

sourceRange.text: 恭帝，諱宗訓，世宗子也。廣順三年，歲在癸丑，八月四日，生於澶州之府第。顯德六年六月癸未，制授特進左衛上將軍，封梁王，食邑三千戶，實封五百戶。癸巳，世宗崩。甲午，內出遺制，命帝柩前即皇帝位。是日，群臣奉帝即位而退。丁酉，北面兵馬都部署韓令坤奏，敗契丹五百騎於霸州北。戊戌，文武百僚、宰臣範質等上表請聽政，表三上，允之。壬寅，文武臣僚上表，請以八月四日為天壽節，從之。癸卯，以司徒、平章事範質為山陵使，以翰林學士、判太常寺事竇儼為禮儀使，以兵部尚書張昭為鹵簿使，以御史中丞邊歸讜為儀仗使，以宣徽南院使、判開封府事昝居潤為橋道頓遞使。是月，州郡十六奏大雨連旬不止。

context.afterSource: 秋七月丁未，以戶部尚書李濤為山陵副使，以度支郎中盧億為山陵判官。
context.afterLocal: 秋七月丁未，以戶部尚書李濤為山陵副使，以度支郎中盧億為山陵判官。

manualTranslations.zh: 恭帝，諱宗訓，世宗子也。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Gong, taboo name Zongxun, was the son of Shizong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong, whose personal name was Zongxun, was Shizong's son.

manualTranslations.zh: 廣順三年，歲在癸丑，八月四日，生於澶州之府第。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year of Guangshun, the year being guichou, on the fourth day of the eighth month, he was born at the official residence in Chanzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangshun (guichou), on the fourth day of the eighth month, he was born at the prefectural residence in Chanzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 顯德六年六月癸未，制授特進左衛上將軍，封梁王，食邑三千戶，實封五百戶。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth year of Xiande, on guiwei of the sixth month, by imperial order he was granted Special Advancement and General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, enfeoffed as Prince of Liang with a fief of three thousand households and an actual seal of five hundred households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Xiande, on guiwei, he was ordered to receive Special Advancement and made General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, enfeoffed as Prince of Liang with a nominal fief of three thousand households and an actual enfeoffment of five hundred.

manualTranslations.zh: 癸巳，世宗崩。
manualTranslations.literal: On guisi, Shizong died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guisi Shizong died.

manualTranslations.zh: 甲午，內出遺制，命帝柩前即皇帝位。
manualTranslations.literal: On jiawu, the late emperor's testament was issued from within the palace, ordering the Emperor to ascend the throne before the coffin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiawu the late emperor's testament was read from within the palace, commanding the heir to take the throne before the coffin.

manualTranslations.zh: 是日，群臣奉帝即位而退。
manualTranslations.literal: That day the ministers presented the Emperor to ascend the throne, then withdrew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That day the ministers presented him for enthronement and then withdrew.

manualTranslations.zh: 丁酉，北面兵馬都部署韓令坤奏，敗契丹五百騎於霸州北。
manualTranslations.literal: On dingyou, Han Lingkun, Director-in-Chief of Northern Armies and Cavalry, memorialized that five hundred Khitan horsemen had been defeated north of Bazhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingyou Han Lingkun, northern armies commissioner, reported defeating five hundred Khitan horsemen north of Bazhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 戊戌，文武百僚、宰臣範質等上表請聽政，表三上，允之。
manualTranslations.literal: On wuxu, the civil and military officials and chief minister Fan Zhi and others submitted a memorial requesting that he assume governance; they submitted three times, and permission was granted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On wuxu Fan Zhi and the civil and military officials submitted three memorials asking him to take up governance, and he assented.

manualTranslations.zh: 壬寅，文武臣僚上表，請以八月四日為天壽節，從之。
manualTranslations.literal: On renyin, civil and military officials submitted a memorial requesting that the fourth day of the eighth month be made the Birthday Festival; the request was accepted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renyin the officials memorialized to make the fourth day of the eighth month the imperial birthday festival, and he agreed.

manualTranslations.zh: 癸卯，以司徒、平章事範質為山陵使，以翰林學士、判太常寺事竇儼為禮儀使，以兵部尚書張昭為鹵簿使，以御史中丞邊歸讜為儀仗使，以宣徽南院使、判開封府事昝居潤為橋道頓遞使。
manualTranslations.literal: On guimao, Fan Zhi, Minister of Education and Councilor of the Second Rank, was made commissioner for the imperial tomb; Dou Yan, Hanlin Academician and Administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made ritual commissioner; Zhang Zhao, Minister of War, was made commissioner for the imperial regalia; Bian Guichan, Vice Censor-in-Chief, was made commissioner for ceremonial arms; and Zan Jurun, Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Directorate and acting Administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture, was made commissioner for bridges, roads, and relay stations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guimao Fan Zhi was named tomb commissioner; Hanlin academician Dou Yan, ritual commissioner; Minister of War Zhang Zhao, regalia commissioner; Vice Censor-in-Chief Bian Guichan, arms commissioner; and acting Kaifeng administrator Zan Jurun, bridges-and-relay commissioner.

manualTranslations.zh: 是月，州郡十六奏大雨連旬不止。
manualTranslations.literal: That month, sixteen prefectures and commanderies reported that heavy rain had continued for more than ten days without stopping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That month sixteen prefectures reported unrelenting heavy rains for more than ten days.

sourceRange.text: 春正月辛丑朔，文武百僚進名奉賀。

localRange.text: 顯德七年春正月辛丑朔，文武百僚進名奉賀。

sourceRange.text: ）史臣曰：周室后妃凡六人，而追冊者四，故中闈內則，罕得而聞，惟董妃、符後之懿範，亦無愧於彤管矣。（案：薛史無外戚傳，考《五代會要》云：周太祖第三女樂安公主，為漢室所害，廣順元年二月追封，至顯德四年四月，又追封莒國長公主。第四女壽安公主，降張永德，廣順元年四月封，至顯德元年，封晉國長公主。第五女永寧公主，廣順元年九月追封，至顯德四年四月，又追封梁國長公主。

context.beforeSource: 世宗素以後賢，又聞命不以出家為念，愈賢之，所以為天下母也。

manualTranslations.zh: 史臣曰：周室后妃凡六人，而追冊者四，故中闈內則，罕得而聞，惟董妃、符後之懿範，亦無愧於彤管矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The historiographer says: The consorts of the Zhou house numbered six in all, of whom four were posthumously invested; hence the inner quarters and household rules are rarely heard of—only the fine models of Lady Dong and Empress Fu are without shame before the red brush.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: The Zhou house had six consorts in all, four of them posthumously invested; little is therefore known of the inner palace and its rules—yet the exemplary conduct of Lady Dong and Empress Fu would not disgrace the red brush.

manualTranslations.zh: 〈（案：薛史無外戚傳，考《五代會要》云：周太祖第三女樂安公主，為漢室所害，廣順元年二月追封，至顯德四年四月，又追封莒國長公主。
manualTranslations.literal: (Note: Xue's History has no biography of maternal kin; consulting the 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》, it states that the third daughter of Emperor Taizu of Zhou, Princess Le'an, was killed by the Han court; she was posthumously enfeoffed in the second month of the first year of Guangshun, and in the fourth month of the fourth year of Xiande was again posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the State of Ju.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: (Note: Xue's History has no biography of maternal kin. The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records that Emperor Taizu's third daughter, Princess Le'an, was killed during the Later Han; she was posthumously enfeoffed in Guangshun 1.2 and again as Grand Princess of Ju in Xiande 4.4.

manualTranslations.zh: 第四女壽安公主，降張永德，廣順元年四月封，至顯德元年，封晉國長公主。
manualTranslations.literal: The fourth daughter, Princess Shou'an, married Zhang Yongde and was enfeoffed in the fourth month of the first year of Guangshun; by the first year of Xiande she was enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the State of Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The fourth daughter, Princess Shou'an, married Zhang Yongde and was enfeoffed in Guangshun 1.4; by Xiande 1 she held the title Grand Princess of Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 第五女永寧公主，廣順元年九月追封，至顯德四年四月，又追封梁國長公主。）〉
manualTranslations.literal: The fifth daughter, Princess Yongning, was posthumously enfeoffed in the ninth month of the first year of Guangshun; by the fourth month of the fourth year of Xiande she was again posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the State of Liang.)〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The fifth daughter, Princess Yongning, was posthumously enfeoffed in Guangshun 1.9 and again as Grand Princess of Liang in Xiande 4.4.)〉

manualTranslations.zh: 妃兄廷璋，蚤事太祖，即位累歷內職，出為晉州節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: The lady's elder brother Tingzhang had long served the Emperor; when he took the throne Tingzhang successively held inner-court posts and was then sent out as military governor of Jin Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Tingzhang had served the Emperor from early on; after the founding he held a series of inner-court posts before being appointed military governor of Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇朝撫運，移鎮邢州，又改鄜州，受代歸闕，卒於私第。
manualTranslations.literal: When the dynasty received Heaven's favor he was transferred to garrison Xing Prefecture, then reassigned to Yan Prefecture; after his term ended he returned to court and died at his private residence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under the new dynasty he was transferred to Xingzhou, then reassigned to Yanzhou; when his term ended he returned to the capital and died at home.

context.afterSource: 杞王信，太祖子，初名意哥，漢末遇害。

sourceRange.text: ）長興初，移鎮宋州。唐末帝起兵於鳳翔，其子重吉為亳州防禦使，從敏承朝廷命害之。清泰中，從敏與洋王從璋並罷歸第，待之甚薄。嘗宮中同飲，既醉，末帝謂從璋、從敏曰：「爾等何物，處雄藩大鎮！」二人大懼，賴曹太后見之，叱曰：「官家醉，爾輩速出去！」方得解。晉祖革命，降封莒國公，再領陜州，尋移鎮上黨，入為右龍武統軍，出為河陽節度使。漢祖入汴，移授西京留守，累官檢校太師、同平章事。隱帝即位，就加兼侍中，改封秦國公。歲餘，以王守恩代還。廣順元年春，以疾卒，年五十四。詔贈中書令，謚曰恭惠。

context.beforeSource: （《北夢瑣言》：從敏初欲削官，中宮哀祈，竟罰一年俸。
context.afterSource: 鄭仁誨，字日新，晉陽人。

manualTranslations.zh: 長興初，移鎮宋州。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Changxing, he was transferred to command Songzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changxing he was transferred to command Songzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 唐末帝起兵於鳳翔，其子重吉為亳州防禦使，從敏承朝廷命害之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Last Emperor of Tang raised troops at Fengxiang, his son Chongji was defense commissioner of Bozhou; Congmin, on court orders, killed him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor of Tang raised troops at Fengxiang, his son Chongji was defense commissioner of Bozhou. On court orders Congmin killed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 清泰中，從敏與洋王從璋並罷歸第，待之甚薄。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Qingtai era, Congmin and Prince Yang Congzhang were both dismissed and sent home, and he was treated very coldly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Qingtai era Congmin and Prince Yang Congzhang were both dismissed and sent home, and he was treated very coldly.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘗宮中同飲，既醉，末帝謂從璋、從敏曰：「爾等何物，處雄藩大鎮！
manualTranslations.literal: Once they drank together in the palace and, when drunk, the Last Emperor said to Congzhang and Congmin, "What sort of things are you, to hold great frontier commands!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once they drank together in the palace and, when drunk, the Last Emperor said to Congzhang and Congmin, "What sort of things are you, to hold great frontier commands!

manualTranslations.zh: 」二人大懼，賴曹太后見之，叱曰：「官家醉，爾輩速出去！
manualTranslations.literal: " The two were greatly afraid. Thanks to Empress Dowager Cao's presence, she rebuked them, saying, "The sovereign is drunk. Get out at once!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " The two were greatly afraid. Thanks to Empress Dowager Cao's presence, she rebuked them, saying, "The sovereign is drunk. Get out at once!

manualTranslations.zh: 」方得解。
manualTranslations.literal: " Only then were they released.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Only then were they released.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉祖革命，降封莒國公，再領陜州，尋移鎮上黨，入為右龍武統軍，出為河陽節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: When the founding emperor of Jin seized power, Congmin was demoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Ju, again took charge of Shanzhou, soon moved to command Shangdang, entered court as commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army, and went out as military commissioner of Heyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor of Jin seized power, Congmin was demoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Ju. He again took charge of Shanzhou, soon moved to command Shangdang, entered court as commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army, and went out as military commissioner of Heyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢祖入汴，移授西京留守，累官檢校太師、同平章事。
manualTranslations.literal: When the founding emperor of Han entered Bian, he was transferred to western capital regent and cumulatively held the posts of honorary Grand Preceptor and co-equal to the Secretariat-Chancellery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor of Han entered Bian, he was made western capital regent and cumulatively held the posts of honorary Grand Preceptor and co-equal to the Secretariat-Chancellery.

manualTranslations.zh: 隱帝即位，就加兼侍中，改封秦國公。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor ascended, he was thereupon additionally made chief minister and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Qin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Emperor ascended, he was thereupon additionally made chief minister and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Qin.

manualTranslations.zh: 歲餘，以王守恩代還。
manualTranslations.literal: After more than a year, Wang Shouen replaced him and he returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After more than a year Wang Shouen replaced him and he returned.

manualTranslations.zh: 廣順元年春，以疾卒，年五十四。
manualTranslations.literal: In spring of the first year of Guangshun, he died of illness at age fifty-four.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of Guangshun he died of illness at age fifty-four.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔贈中書令，謚曰恭惠。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict posthumously honored him as Director of the Secretariat; his posthumous title was Gonghui.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously honored him as Director of the Secretariat. His posthumous title was Gonghui.

sourceRange.text: 」漢高祖入汴，加守太傅、兼中書令，代李守貞為天平節度使。杜重威據鄴叛，漢祖以行周為招討使，總兵討之。鄴平，授鄴都留守，加守太尉，進爵臨清王。乾祐中，入覲，加守太師，進封鄴王，復授天平節鉞，改封齊王。太祖踐阼，加守尚書令，增食邑至一萬七千戶。太祖以行周耆年宿將，賜詔不名，但呼王位而已。慕容彥超據兗叛，太祖親征，奉迎輿駕，傾家載贄，奉觴進俎，率以身先，太祖待之逾厚。廣順二年秋，以疾薨於位，享年六十八。赗賻加等，冊贈尚書令，追封秦王，謚曰武懿。

context.beforeSource: ）及契丹主死於欒城，契丹將蕭翰立許王李從益知南朝軍國事，遣死士召行周，辭之以疾，退謂人曰：「衰世難輔，況兒戲乎！
context.afterSource: 子懷德，皇朝駙馬都尉、宋州節度使。

manualTranslations.zh: 」漢高祖入汴，加守太傅、兼中書令，代李守貞為天平節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Han entered Bian, Xingzhou was made acting Grand Tutor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, replacing Li Shouzhen as military commissioner of the Pingping circuit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu of Han entered Bian, Xingzhou was made acting Grand Tutor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, replacing Li Shouzhen as military commissioner of the Pingping circuit.

manualTranslations.zh: 杜重威據鄴叛，漢祖以行周為招討使，總兵討之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Du Chongwei held Ye and rebelled, the founding emperor of Han made Xingzhou pacification commissioner and entrusted him with total command to suppress the rebellion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Du Chongwei held Ye and rebelled, the founding emperor of Han made Xingzhou pacification commissioner and entrusted him with total command to suppress the rebellion.

manualTranslations.zh: 鄴平，授鄴都留守，加守太尉，進爵臨清王。
manualTranslations.literal: After Ye was pacified, he was made regent of the Ye capital, made acting Grand Commandant, and advanced in rank to Prince of Linqing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Ye was pacified, he was made regent of the Ye capital, made acting Grand Commandant, and advanced in rank to Prince of Linqing.

manualTranslations.zh: 乾祐中，入覲，加守太師，進封鄴王，復授天平節鉞，改封齊王。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Qianyou era he came to court, was made acting Grand Preceptor, was advanced to Prince of Ye, was again granted the Pingping commissioner seal and command, and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Qianyou era he came to court, was made acting Grand Preceptor, was advanced to Prince of Ye, was again granted the Pingping commissioner seal and command, and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖踐阼，加守尚書令，增食邑至一萬七千戶。
manualTranslations.literal: When the founding emperor took the throne, Xingzhou was made acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and his stipendary households were increased to seventeen thousand.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor took the throne, Xingzhou was made acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and his stipendary households were increased to seventeen thousand.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖以行周耆年宿將，賜詔不名，但呼王位而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Because Xingzhou was an old commander of advanced years, the founding emperor granted an edict that he should not be named in summons but addressed only by his princely title.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because Xingzhou was an old commander of advanced years, the founding emperor granted an edict that he should not be named in summons but addressed only by his princely title.

manualTranslations.zh: 慕容彥超據兗叛，太祖親征，奉迎輿駕，傾家載贄，奉觴進俎，率以身先，太祖待之逾厚。
manualTranslations.literal: When Murong Yanchao held Yan and rebelled, the founding emperor campaigned in person. Xingzhou came out to welcome the imperial carriage, emptied his household to load tribute gifts, offered cups and served viands, always leading by personal example, and the founding emperor treated him with still greater favor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Murong Yanchao held Yan and rebelled, the founding emperor campaigned in person. Xingzhou came out to welcome the imperial carriage, emptied his household to load tribute gifts, offered cups and served viands, always leading by personal example, and the founding emperor treated him with still greater favor.

manualTranslations.zh: 廣順二年秋，以疾薨於位，享年六十八。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Guangshun he died in office of illness at age sixty-eight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In autumn of the second year of Guangshun he died in office of illness at age sixty-eight.

manualTranslations.zh: 赗賻加等，冊贈尚書令，追封秦王，謚曰武懿。
manualTranslations.literal: Funeral gifts were increased by one grade. By patent he was posthumously honored as Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Qin, and given the posthumous title Wuyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts were increased by one grade. By patent he was posthumously honored as Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Qin, and given the posthumous title Wuyi.

sourceRange.text: 王進，幽州良鄉人。少落魄，不事生業，為人勇悍，走及奔馬，嘗聚黨為盜，封境患之。符彥超為河朔郡守，以賂誘置之左右。長興初，彥超鎮安州，屬部曲王希全構亂軍州，令進賫變狀聞於朝廷，明宗賞其捷足，詔隸於軍中。洎契丹內寇，戰於膠口，進獨追擒六十七人，時漢祖總侍衛親軍，知其驍果，擢為馬前親校。漢祖鎮河東，或邊上警急，令進賫封章達於闕下，自並至汴，不六七日復焉，由是恩撫頗厚。繼任戎職，累遷至奉國軍都指揮使。從太祖入平內難，以功遷虎捷右廂都指揮使，歷汝、鄭防禦使，亦有政聲。俄授相州節度使，為政之道頓減於前，議者惜之。顯德元年秋，以疾卒於任。贈檢校太師。

context.beforeSource: 子延欽，仕皇朝為控鶴廂使。
context.afterSource: 史彥超，雲州人也。
context.beforeLocal: 子延欽，仕皇朝為控鶴廂使。
context.afterLocal: 史彥超，雲州人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 王進，幽州良鄉人。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Jin was a man of Liangxiang in You Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Jin was a native of Liangxiang in You Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 少落魄，不事生業，為人勇悍，走及奔馬，嘗聚黨為盜，封境患之。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth he was down and out and did not pursue any livelihood; he was brave and fierce by nature, could run as fast as a galloping horse, and once gathered a band to serve as bandits, which troubled the frontier district.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In youth he was destitute and idle, fierce and fearless, and could keep pace with a galloping horse. He once led a band of robbers, to the dismay of the frontier district.

manualTranslations.zh: 符彥超為河朔郡守，以賂誘置之左右。
manualTranslations.literal: Fu Yanchao was prefect of a commandery north of the Yellow River and, with bribes, lured him to keep him at his side.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Fu Yanchao was a prefect in Hebei, he bribed Wang Jin and brought him into his retinue.

manualTranslations.zh: 長興初，彥超鎮安州，屬部曲王希全構亂軍州，令進賫變狀聞於朝廷，明宗賞其捷足，詔隸於軍中。
manualTranslations.literal: Early in Changxing, Yanchao commanded An Prefecture; when his subordinate Wang Xiquan stirred rebellion in the army and prefecture, he had Jin carry an emergency report to court; Mingzong praised his swift feet and ordered him enrolled in the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Early in the Changxing period Yanchao took command of An Prefecture. When his subordinate Wang Xiquan stirred rebellion in the army and prefecture, he had Jin carry an emergency report to court. Mingzong praised his swift feet and ordered him enrolled in the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 洎契丹內寇，戰於膠口，進獨追擒六十七人，時漢祖總侍衛親軍，知其驍果，擢為馬前親校。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Khitans invaded, at Jiaokou Jin alone pursued and captured sixty-seven men; at that time the Han founder commanded the imperial guard, knew his valor, and promoted him to personal attendant before his horse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Khitans invaded and battle was joined at Jiaokou, Jin alone pursued and captured sixty-seven men. The founder of Later Han then commanded the imperial guard; recognizing Jin's valor, he promoted him to personal attendant before his horse.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢祖鎮河東，或邊上警急，令進賫封章達於闕下，自並至汴，不六七日復焉，由是恩撫頗厚。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Han founder held Hedong, whenever the border was urgently alarmed he had Jin carry sealed memorials to the court; from Bing to Bian and back took no more than six or seven days, and from this his favor and care were quite generous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Han founder held Hedong and border emergencies arose, he had Jin carry sealed memorials to the capital. From Bing to Bian and back took no more than six or seven days, and from this he won substantial favor.

manualTranslations.zh: 繼任戎職，累遷至奉國軍都指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: He continued in military office and was repeatedly promoted to commander of the Fengguo army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He continued in military service and rose through repeated promotions to commander of the Fengguo army.

manualTranslations.zh: 從太祖入平內難，以功遷虎捷右廂都指揮使，歷汝、鄭防禦使，亦有政聲。
manualTranslations.literal: He followed the Taizu in entering to settle the inner crisis; for merit he was transferred to commander of the right wing of the Hujie army, served as defense commissioner of Ru and Zheng prefectures, and also had a reputation for good governance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He followed Taizu into the capital to settle the internal crisis and was transferred for merit to commander of the right wing of the Hujie army. He served as defense commissioner of Ru and Zheng prefectures and also won a reputation for good governance.

manualTranslations.zh: 俄授相州節度使，為政之道頓減於前，議者惜之。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he was appointed military governor of Xiang Prefecture; his way of governing abruptly declined from before, and discussants regretted it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed military governor of Xiang Prefecture, but his governing noticeably declined from before, to observers' regret.

manualTranslations.zh: 顯德元年秋，以疾卒於任。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn of the first year of Xiande he died of illness in his post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Xiande he died of illness in office.

manualTranslations.zh: 贈檢校太師。
manualTranslations.literal: Posthumously granted Acting Grand Master.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the acting title of Grand Master.

sourceRange.text: 周密，字德峰，應州神武川人也。初事後唐武皇為軍職。莊宗之平常山，明宗之襲汶陽，密皆從征有功。莊宗平梁，授鎮州馬軍都指揮使。明宗即位，累遷河東馬步軍副都指揮使。晉天福初，除冀州刺史，累官至檢校司徒，入為右羽林統軍、檢校太保。四年秋，授保大軍節度使、檢校太傅。屬部民作亂，密討平之，尋移鎮晉州，加檢校太尉。開運中，入拜右龍武統軍。三年秋，出鎮延州。其年冬，契丹陷中原，延州軍亂，立高允權為帥，時密據東城，允權據西城，相拒久之。會漢高祖建義於太原，遣使安撫，密乃棄其城奔於太原，隨漢祖歸汴，久居於闕下。廣順初，授太子太師致仕。顯德元年春卒，時年七十五。

context.beforeSource: 顯德三年夏，以疾卒，時年六十有二，詔贈侍中。
context.afterSource: 長子銳，仕皇朝為內職。
context.beforeLocal: 顯德三年夏，以疾卒，時年六十有二，詔贈侍中。
context.afterLocal: 長子銳，仕皇朝為內職。

manualTranslations.zh: 周密，字德峰，應州神武川人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhou Mi, courtesy name Defeng, was a man of Shenwuchuan in Ying Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhou Mi, whose courtesy name was Defeng, was a native of Shenwuchuan in Ying Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 初事後唐武皇為軍職。
manualTranslations.literal: He first served Later Tang's Martial Emperor in a military post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He first served the Martial Emperor of Later Tang in a military post.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗之平常山，明宗之襲汶陽，密皆從征有功。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Changshan and when Mingzong raided Wenyang, Mi followed both campaigns with merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Changshan and when Mingzong raided Wenyang, Mi followed both campaigns with merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗平梁，授鎮州馬軍都指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Mi was appointed commander of the mounted army of Zhen Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Liang, he was appointed commander of the mounted army of Zhen Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗即位，累遷河東馬步軍副都指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Mi was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Hedong mounted and infantry armies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingzong came to the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Hedong mounted and infantry armies.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉天福初，除冀州刺史，累官至檢校司徒，入為右羽林統軍、檢校太保。
manualTranslations.literal: Early in Jin Tianfu he was made prefect of Ji Prefecture, rose through repeated offices to Acting Minister of Education, and entered court as commander of the Right Yulin Guard and Acting Grand Guardian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin Tianfu period he was made prefect of Ji Prefecture, rose through repeated offices to Acting Minister of Education, and entered court as commander of the Right Yulin Guard with the acting title of Grand Guardian.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年秋，授保大軍節度使、檢校太傅。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn of the fourth year he was appointed military governor of the Baoda army and Acting Grand Tutor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year he was appointed military governor of the Baoda army and Acting Grand Tutor.

manualTranslations.zh: 屬部民作亂，密討平之，尋移鎮晉州，加檢校太尉。
manualTranslations.literal: When local people rebelled, Mi suppressed and pacified them; soon he was transferred to command Jin Prefecture and given the added Acting Grand Commandant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When local people rebelled, Mi suppressed them. Soon he was transferred to command Jin Prefecture and given the acting title of Grand Commandant.

manualTranslations.zh: 開運中，入拜右龍武統軍。
manualTranslations.literal: During Kaiyun he entered court and was appointed commander of the Right Longwu Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyun period he entered court and was appointed commander of the Right Longwu Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年秋，出鎮延州。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn of the third year he went out to command Yan Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year he went out to command Yan Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 其年冬，契丹陷中原，延州軍亂，立高允權為帥，時密據東城，允權據西城，相拒久之。
manualTranslations.literal: That winter the Khitans seized the Central Plains; the Yanzhou army rebelled and set up Gao Yunquan as commander; at that time Mi held the eastern city and Yunquan held the western city, and they opposed each other for a long time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That winter the Khitans overran the Central Plains. The Yanzhou army rebelled and made Gao Yunquan commander. Mi held the eastern city and Yunquan the western city, and they opposed each other for a long time.

manualTranslations.zh: 會漢高祖建義於太原，遣使安撫，密乃棄其城奔於太原，隨漢祖歸汴，久居於闕下。
manualTranslations.literal: When Han Gaozu raised his standard at Taiyuan and sent envoys to reassure him, Mi then abandoned his city and fled to Taiyuan, followed the Han founder back to Bian, and lived long at court.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu raised his standard at Taiyuan and sent envoys to reassure him, Mi abandoned his city and fled to Taiyuan. He followed the founder of Later Han back to Bian and lived long at court.

manualTranslations.zh: 廣順初，授太子太師致仕。
manualTranslations.literal: Early in Guangshun he was appointed Prince Tutor and retired.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun period he was made Prince Tutor and retired from office.

manualTranslations.zh: 顯德元年春卒，時年七十五。
manualTranslations.literal: He died in spring of the first year of Xiande, aged seventy-five.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in the spring of the first year of Xiande, aged seventy-five.

sourceRange.text: 其弟行友繼為定州節度。皇朝乾德中，以其妖妄惑眾，詔毀狼山佛寺，遷其尼朽骨赴京，遣焚於北郊，以行友為諸衛大將軍，自是祅徒遂息焉。（《續通鑒長編》：建隆二年八月，義成節度使、同平章事孫行友，在鎮逾八年，而狼山妖尼深意黨益盛。上初即位，行友不自安，累表乞解官歸山，上不許，行友懼，乃繕治甲兵，將棄其帑，還據山寨以叛。兵馬都監樂繼能密奏其事，上遣閣門副使武懷節馳騎會鎮、趙之兵，偽稱巡邊，直入定州，行友不之覺。既而出詔示之，令舉族歸朝，行友倉皇聽命。既至，命侍御史李維嶽即訊得實。己酉，制削奪行友官爵，禁錮私第，取尼深意屍，焚之都城西北隅。行友弟易州刺史方進、侄保塞軍使全暉，皆詣闕待罪，詔釋之。

context.beforeSource: 輟視朝兩日，詔贈太師。
context.afterSource: ）史臣曰：昔晉之季也，敵騎長驅，中原無主，漢祖雖思拯溺，未果圖南。

manualTranslations.zh: 皇朝乾德中，以其妖妄惑眾，詔毀狼山佛寺，遷其尼朽骨赴京，遣焚於北郊，以行友為諸衛大將軍，自是祅徒遂息焉。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Qiande reign of the imperial dynasty, because the cult deluded the people with false and extravagant claims, an edict ordered the Langshan Buddhist monastery destroyed, the rotted bones of its nun transported to the capital and burned in the northern suburbs, and Xingyou made a general-in-chief of the Palace Guard; from then on the heterodox followers ceased their activities.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Qiande reign of the Song dynasty, because the cult had deluded the people with false claims, an edict ordered the Langshan Buddhist monastery destroyed. The rotted bones of the nun were transported to the capital and burned in the northern suburbs, and Xingyou was made a general-in-chief of the Palace Guard. From then on the heterodox followers ceased their activities.

manualTranslations.zh: （《續通鑒長編》：建隆二年八月，義成節度使、同平章事孫行友，在鎮逾八年，而狼山妖尼深意黨益盛。
manualTranslations.literal: (From the Extended Comprehensive Mirror: In the eighth month of the second year of Jianlong, Sun Xingyou, military governor of Yicheng and concurrent Director of the Chancellery, had been in his post for more than eight years, while the Langshan sorceress Shenyi and her faction grew ever stronger.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: (From the Extended Comprehensive Mirror: In the eighth month of the second year of Jianlong, Sun Xingyou, military governor of Yicheng and concurrent Director of the Chancellery, had held his post for more than eight years, while the Langshan sorceress Shenyi and her faction grew ever stronger.

manualTranslations.zh: 上初即位，行友不自安，累表乞解官歸山，上不許，行友懼，乃繕治甲兵，將棄其帑，還據山寨以叛。
manualTranslations.literal: When the emperor had just succeeded to the throne, Xingyou felt insecure; he repeatedly memorialized begging to resign his office and return to the mountains; the emperor did not permit it; Xingyou grew afraid and therefore repaired armor and weapons, intending to abandon his treasury, return to hold a mountain stockade, and rebel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the emperor had just succeeded to the throne, Xingyou felt insecure. He repeatedly memorialized asking to resign and return to the mountains, but the emperor refused. Xingyou grew afraid and began repairing armor and weapons, intending to abandon his treasury, return to a mountain stockade, and rebel.

manualTranslations.zh: 兵馬都監樂繼能密奏其事，上遣閣門副使武懷節馳騎會鎮、趙之兵，偽稱巡邊，直入定州，行友不之覺。
manualTranslations.literal: The army-and-horse supervisory commissioner Yue Jineng secretly memorialized about the matter; the emperor sent Vice Commissioner of the Inner Gate Wu Huaijie riding at speed to join the forces of Zhen and Zhao, falsely claiming a frontier inspection, and entered Dingzhou directly; Xingyou did not detect it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The army-and-horse supervisory commissioner Yue Jineng secretly reported the matter. The emperor sent Vice Commissioner of the Inner Gate Wu Huaijie riding at speed to join the forces of Zhen and Zhao, falsely claiming a frontier inspection, and entered Dingzhou directly. Xingyou did not detect it.

manualTranslations.zh: 既而出詔示之，令舉族歸朝，行友倉皇聽命。
manualTranslations.literal: Then an edict was produced and shown to him, ordering his whole clan to return to court; Xingyou in panic obeyed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then an edict was produced and shown to him, ordering his whole clan to return to court. Xingyou obeyed in panic.

manualTranslations.zh: 既至，命侍御史李維嶽即訊得實。
manualTranslations.literal: Once he arrived, Attending Censor Li Weiyue was ordered to question him on the spot and the facts were established.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, Attending Censor Li Weiyue was ordered to question him on the spot, and the facts were established.

manualTranslations.zh: 己酉，制削奪行友官爵，禁錮私第，取尼深意屍，焚之都城西北隅。
manualTranslations.literal: On jiyou day, an imperial order stripped Xingyou of his offices and titles, confined him in his private residence, took the corpse of the nun Shenyi, and burned it in the northwest corner of the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiyou day, an imperial order stripped Xingyou of his offices and titles and confined him in his private residence. The corpse of the nun Shenyi was taken and burned in the northwest corner of the capital.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xingyou's younger brother Fangjin, prefect of Yizhou, and his nephew Quanhui, commissioner of Baosai Army, all came to court to await punishment. An edict pardoned them.)

sourceRange.text: 晉祖入洛，罷相為吏部尚書，再遷太子少傅。少帝嗣位，改太子太傅。漢祖登極，轉太子太師。時朝官分司在洛，雖有留臺御史，紀綱亦多不整肅，遂敕文紀別令檢轄。侍御史趙礪及糾分司朝臣中有行香拜表疏怠者，楊邠怒，凡疾病不在朝謁者，皆與致仕官。時文紀別令檢轄之職，頗甚滋章，因疾請假，復為留臺所奏，遂以本官致仕。（《歐陽史》：周太祖入立，即拜司空於家。）廣順元年夏卒，年七十六。贈司徒，輟視朝一日。文紀平生積財巨萬，及卒，為其子龜齡所費，不數年間，以至蕩盡，由是多藏者以為誡焉。

manualTranslations.literal: When the Jin Ancestor entered Luoyang, Wenji was removed from the chief ministership and made Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted again to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Jin founder entered Luoyang, Wenji left the chief ministership for director of the Ministry of Personnel, then was promoted again to junior tutor of the heir.

manualTranslations.zh: 少帝嗣位，改太子太傅。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was changed to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made grand tutor of the heir.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢祖登極，轉太子太師。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Han founder ascended the throne, he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Han founder took the throne, he became grand mentor of the heir.

manualTranslations.zh: 時朝官分司在洛，雖有留臺御史，紀綱亦多不整肅，遂敕文紀別令檢轄。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time court officials with branch offices in Luoyang had leave-behind censors, yet discipline was often not strict; Wenji was therefore ordered to serve separately as special inspector.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Court officials then held branch offices in Luoyang. Though leave-behind censors existed, discipline was often lax, so Wenji was ordered to serve separately as special inspector.

manualTranslations.zh: 侍御史趙礪及糾分司朝臣中有行香拜表疏怠者，楊邠怒，凡疾病不在朝謁者，皆與致仕官。
manualTranslations.literal: Attending Censor Zhao Li and others impeached Luoyang branch officials lax in incense rites and memorial audiences. Yang Bin grew angry and granted retirement to all who claimed illness and stayed away from court audiences.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Zhao Li and others impeached Luoyang branch officials lax in incense rites and memorial audiences. Yang Bin grew angry and granted retirement to all who claimed illness and stayed away from court audiences.

manualTranslations.zh: 時文紀別令檢轄之職，頗甚滋章，因疾請假，復為留臺所奏，遂以本官致仕。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Wenji's duties as special inspector grew increasingly burdensome. Taking sick leave, he was again impeached by the leave-behind office and retired at his original rank.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wenji's special inspection duties grew increasingly burdensome. After he took sick leave, the leave-behind office impeached him again, and he retired at his original rank.

manualTranslations.zh: （《歐陽史》：周太祖入立，即拜司空於家。）
manualTranslations.literal: (The History of Ouyang: When Zhou Taizu took power, Wenji was at once appointed Grand Master of Works at home.)
manualTranslations.idiomatic: (The History of Ouyang: When Zhou Taizu took power, Wenji was at once appointed Grand Master of Works at home.)

manualTranslations.zh: 廣順元年夏卒，年七十六。
manualTranslations.literal: He died in summer of the first year of Guangshun, aged seventy-six.

manualTranslations.zh: 贈司徒，輟視朝一日。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister over the masses and court audience was suspended one day.

manualTranslations.zh: 文紀平生積財巨萬，及卒，為其子龜齡所費，不數年間，以至蕩盡，由是多藏者以為誡焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Wenji had amassed great wealth in life; after his death his son Guiling spent it all within a few years until nothing remained—whereafter many hoarders took this as a warning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wenji had amassed great wealth in life, but after his death his son Guiling spent it within a few years until nothing remained, and many hoarders thereafter took this as a warning.

sourceRange.text: 緯以撰述之勞，每詣宰執，懇祈遷轉，遇內難不果。太祖即位，改給事中，判館如故。先是，竇貞固奏請修晉朝實錄，既竟，亦望升擢。貞固猶在相位，乃上疏抗論除拜不平。既而以所撰日曆示監修王峻，皆媒孽貞固及蘇禹珪之短，歷詆朝士之先達者。峻惡之，謂同列曰：「賈給事家有士子，亦要門閥無玷，今滿朝並遭非毀，教士子何以進身！」乃於太祖前言之，出為平盧軍行軍司馬。時符彥卿鎮青州，以緯文士，厚禮之。緯妻以緯左遷，駭惋傷離，病留於京。緯書候之曰：「勉醫藥，來春與子同歸獲鹿。」廣順二年春，緯卒。及訃至，妻一慟而終，果雙柩北歸，聞者嘆之。緯有集三十卷，目曰《草堂集》，並聽撰《唐年補錄》六十五卷，皆傳於世。

manualTranslations.zh: 緯以撰述之勞，每詣宰執，懇祈遷轉，遇內難不果。
manualTranslations.literal: For his labors in composition, Wei often visited the chief ministers and earnestly sought transfer and promotion, but when domestic mourning occurred it did not come to pass.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For his labors in composition, Wei often visited the chief ministers and earnestly sought transfer and promotion, but domestic mourning prevented it.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖即位，改給事中，判館如故。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Taizu took the throne, Wei was made attendant gentleman and continued his concurrent duty as director of the academy as before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu took the throne, Wei was made attendant gentleman and continued his concurrent duty directing the academy as before.

manualTranslations.zh: 先是，竇貞固奏請修晉朝實錄，既竟，亦望升擢。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, Dou Zhengu had memorialized requesting the compilation of Jin dynasty Veritable Records; when that was finished, he too hoped for promotion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, Dou Zhengu had memorialized to compile the Jin dynasty Veritable Records; when that was finished, he too hoped for promotion.

manualTranslations.zh: 貞固猶在相位，乃上疏抗論除拜不平。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhengu was still in the chancellorship, so Wei submitted a memorial arguing forcefully that appointments were unfair.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhengu was still chancellor, so Wei submitted a memorial arguing forcefully that appointments were unfair.

manualTranslations.zh: 既而以所撰日曆示監修王峻，皆媒孽貞固及蘇禹珪之短，歷詆朝士之先達者。
manualTranslations.literal: He then showed the calendar he had compiled to supervising compiler Wang Jun; it all slandered the faults of Zhengu and Su Yugui and reviled in turn the senior court officials.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then showed the calendar he had compiled to supervising compiler Wang Jun; it all slandered the faults of Zhengu and Su Yugui and reviled senior court officials in turn.

manualTranslations.zh: 峻惡之，謂同列曰：「賈給事家有士子，亦要門閥無玷，今滿朝並遭非毀，教士子何以進身！」
manualTranslations.literal: Jun resented this and said to his colleagues, "Attendant Gentleman Jia has a scholar-son at home and also values a family name without stain. Now the whole court is being slandered together—how can scholar-sons advance themselves!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jun resented this and said to his colleagues, "Attendant Gentleman Jia has a scholar-son at home and also values an unstained family name. Now the whole court is being slandered together—how can scholar-sons advance themselves!"

manualTranslations.zh: 乃於太祖前言之，出為平盧軍行軍司馬。
manualTranslations.literal: He then spoke of it before Emperor Taizu, and Wei was demoted to acting army marshal of the Pinglu Army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then spoke of it before Emperor Taizu, and Wei was demoted to acting army marshal of the Pinglu Army.

manualTranslations.zh: 時符彥卿鎮青州，以緯文士，厚禮之。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Fu Yanqing was stationed at Qing Prefecture; regarding Wei as a literary gentleman, he treated him with great courtesy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time Fu Yanqing was stationed at Qing Prefecture; regarding Wei as a literary gentleman, he treated him with great courtesy.

manualTranslations.zh: 緯妻以緯左遷，駭惋傷離，病留於京。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei's wife, because of his demotion, was alarmed and grieved at parting; she fell ill and remained in the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because of Wei's demotion, his wife was alarmed and grieved at parting; she fell ill and remained in the capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 緯書候之曰：「勉醫藥，來春與子同歸獲鹿。」
manualTranslations.literal: Wei wrote to inquire after her, saying, "Take medicine diligently; next spring I shall return with our son to Huolu."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei wrote to inquire after her, saying, "Take medicine diligently; next spring I shall return with our son to Huolu."

manualTranslations.zh: 廣順二年春，緯卒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Guangshun, Wei died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Guangshun, Wei died.

manualTranslations.zh: 及訃至，妻一慟而終，果雙柩北歸，聞者嘆之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the death notice arrived, his wife died in a single fit of grief; indeed the two coffins were borne north together, and those who heard of it sighed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the death notice arrived, his wife died in a single fit of grief; the two coffins were indeed borne north together, and those who heard of it sighed.

manualTranslations.zh: 緯有集三十卷，目曰《草堂集》，並聽撰《唐年補錄》六十五卷，皆傳於世。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei left a collected works in thirty juan entitled 《Record of the Thatched Hall》, and was also permitted to compile the 《Supplementary Record of Tang Years》 in sixty-five juan; both circulated in the world.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei left a collected works in thirty juan entitled 《Record of the Thatched Hall》, and was also permitted to compile the 《Supplementary Record of Tang Years》 in sixty-five juan; both circulated in the world.

manualTranslations.literal: Congchang was Maozhen's second son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Congchang was Maozhen's second son.

manualTranslations.zh: 十餘歲署本道中軍使。
manualTranslations.literal: At over ten sui he was appointed Middle Army Commissioner of the circuit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At a little over ten he was appointed middle army commissioner of the circuit.

manualTranslations.zh: 後唐同光中，茂貞疾，從昶年十五，遣代兄從嚴為涇州兩使留後，朝廷尋加節制。
manualTranslations.literal: During Tongguang of Later Tang, Maozhen fell ill; Congchang was fifteen, and was sent to replace his elder brother Congyan as acting commissioner of both civil and military affairs in Jing Prefecture; the court soon added control of the garrison.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Later Tang Tongguang, when Maozhen fell ill, the fifteen-year-old Congchang was sent to replace his elder brother Congyan as acting commissioner of Jingzhou, and the court soon invested him with full control.

manualTranslations.zh: 天成中，明宗即位，改鎮三峰，累官至檢校太保。
manualTranslations.literal: During Tiancheng, when Emperor Mingzong ascended the throne, he was transferred to govern Sanfeng and rose through successive posts to acting Grand Guardian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng, when Mingzong took the throne, he was reassigned to Sanfeng and eventually rose to acting Grand Guardian.

manualTranslations.zh: 會郊天大禮，表請入覲，以恩加檢校太傅。
manualTranslations.literal: When the suburban rites to Heaven were performed, he memorialized requesting an audience at court, and by grace was promoted to acting Grand Mentor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifices to Heaven he petitioned for an audience and was promoted to acting Grand Mentor as a mark of favor.

manualTranslations.zh: 俄有代歸闕，授左驍衛上將軍，改右龍武統軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon a replacement arrived and he returned to court; he was appointed general-in-chief of the Left Yao Guards and then transferred to command the Right Longwu Guards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When a replacement arrived he returned to court, was made general-in-chief of the Left Yao Guards, and then transferred to command the Right Longwu Guards.

manualTranslations.zh: 未幾，出鎮許田，在鎮三年。
manualTranslations.literal: Before long he went out to govern Xutian and governed there three years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before long he was posted to govern Xutian, where he served three years.

manualTranslations.zh: 清泰中，復入為右龍武統軍，再遷左龍武統軍。
manualTranslations.literal: During Qingtai he again entered court service as commander of the Right Longwu Guards and was again transferred to command the Left Longwu Guards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Qingtai he returned to court as commander of the Right Longwu Guards and was later transferred to the Left Longwu Guards.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉天福三年冬，卒於官，時年四十。
manualTranslations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Tianfu of Jin he died in office; he was forty years old.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in office in the winter of the third year of Jin Tianfu, aged forty.

manualTranslations.zh: 贈太尉。
manualTranslations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Grand Commandant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant.

sourceRange.text: 馬希範常重一僧，號報慈長老，能入定觀人休咎。希範因問之曰：「吾於富貴，固無遺恨，但不知者壽爾。吾師以為何如？」報慈曰：「大王無憂，當與佛齊年。」希範喜，以為享壽無窮，及薨也，止於四十九。先是，希範常嫉高郁之為人，因莊宗言而殺之，至是方臨江觀競渡，置酒未及飲，而希範忽驚起，顧其弟曰：「高郁來！」希廣亦驚曰：「高郁死久矣，大王勿妄言！」而希範血自鼻出，是夕遂卒。

context.beforeSource: 」言訖，虎銜二子趨出穴，至行之所感也如此。

manualTranslations.zh: 馬希範常重一僧，號報慈長老，能入定觀人休咎。
manualTranslations.literal: Ma Xifan greatly esteemed a monk styled Elder Baoci, who could enter deep meditation and observe people's fortunes and misfortunes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ma Xifan greatly esteemed a monk called Elder Baoci, who could enter deep meditation and discern people's fortunes and misfortunes.

manualTranslations.zh: 希範因問之曰：「吾於富貴，固無遺恨，但不知者壽爾。
manualTranslations.literal: Xifan therefore asked him, saying: "As to wealth and honor, I truly have no regrets left; only my lifespan is unknown.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xifan asked him, "As for wealth and rank, I have no regrets; only my lifespan is unknown.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾師以為何如？」
manualTranslations.literal: What does my teacher think of this?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What does my teacher think?"

manualTranslations.zh: 報慈曰：「大王無憂，當與佛齊年。」
manualTranslations.literal: Baoci said: "Great King, have no worry—you will live as long as the Buddha."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Baoci said, "Great King, have no worry—you will live as long as the Buddha."

manualTranslations.zh: 希範喜，以為享壽無窮，及薨也，止於四十九。
manualTranslations.literal: Xifan rejoiced, thinking he would enjoy endless years; yet when he died, he was only forty-nine.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xifan rejoiced, thinking he would live forever; yet when he died he was only forty-nine.

manualTranslations.zh: 先是，希範常嫉高郁之為人，因莊宗言而殺之，至是方臨江觀競渡，置酒未及飲，而希範忽驚起，顧其弟曰：「高郁來！」
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier Xifan had always resented Gao Yu's conduct and, because of Zhuangzong's words, had killed him. Now, as he was watching the boat races along the river and had set out wine but not yet drunk, Xifan suddenly started up in alarm, turned to his brother, and said: "Gao Yu has come!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier Xifan had resented Gao Yu and, prompted by Zhuangzong's words, had killed him. Now, as he watched boat races along the river with wine set out but not yet drunk, Xifan suddenly leapt up in alarm, turned to his brother, and cried, "Gao Yu is here!"

manualTranslations.zh: 希廣亦驚曰：「高郁死久矣，大王勿妄言！」
manualTranslations.literal: Xiguang was also alarmed and said: "Gao Yu has been dead a long time—Great King, do not speak rashly!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiguang was alarmed too and said, "Gao Yu has been dead a long time—Great King, do not speak rashly!"

manualTranslations.zh: 而希範血自鼻出，是夕遂卒。
manualTranslations.literal: Then blood issued from Xifan's nose, and that night he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Blood then poured from Xifan's nose, and that night he died.

sourceRange.text: 石文德，連州人。形質矬陋，好學，尤工詩。霸國時，屢獻詩求用，文昭以其寢陋，未曾禮待，文德由是窮悴。有南宅王子者，素重士，延於門下，其後文昭知之，亦兼怒王宅，欲庭辱文德而逐之。居無何，秦國夫人彭氏薨，文昭傷悼，乃命有文學者各撰挽詞，文德亦獻十餘篇，其一聯云：「月沈湘浦冷，花謝漢宮秋。」文昭覽之大驚，曰：「文德有此作用，吾但以寢陋而輕之，乃不如南宮小兒卻能知賢耶！」於是始召文德而愧謝之。未幾，承制授水部員外郎，充融州刺史。文德晚尤好著述，乃撰《大唐新纂》十三卷，多名人遺事，詞雖不工，事或可采，時以多聞許之。

manualTranslations.zh: 石文德，連州人。
manualTranslations.literal: Shi Wendde was a man of Lianzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shi Wendde was from Lianzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 形質矬陋，好學，尤工詩。
manualTranslations.literal: Short and ugly in form, he loved learning and was especially skilled at poetry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Short and homely in appearance, he loved learning and was especially skilled at poetry.

manualTranslations.zh: 霸國時，屢獻詩求用，文昭以其寢陋，未曾禮待，文德由是窮悴。
manualTranslations.literal: During the hegemonic state he repeatedly presented poems seeking employment, but Wenzhao, because he was homely in sleep, never treated him with courtesy; Wendde was thereby reduced to poverty and distress.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the kingdom's rise he repeatedly submitted poems seeking office, but Wenzhao, finding him homely, never treated him courteously, and Wendde fell into poverty.

manualTranslations.zh: 有南宅王子者，素重士，延於門下，其後文昭知之，亦兼怒王宅，欲庭辱文德而逐之。
manualTranslations.literal: There was a prince of the Southern Residence who had always valued scholars and kept Wendde in his household. Later Wenzhao learned of it and was also angry at the prince's residence, wishing to humiliate Wendde in open court and drive him away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A prince of the Southern Residence, who had always valued scholars, took Wendde into his household. When Wenzhao learned of this he was angry at the prince's residence as well and wished to humiliate Wendde in open court and drive him out.

manualTranslations.zh: 居無何，秦國夫人彭氏薨，文昭傷悼，乃命有文學者各撰挽詞，文德亦獻十餘篇，其一聯云：「月沈湘浦冷，花謝漢宮秋。」
manualTranslations.literal: Before long Lady Peng, Lady of Qin, died. Wenzhao mourned and ordered men of letters each to compose elegiac verses; Wendde also presented more than ten pieces, one couplet reading: "The moon sinks cold at the Xiang shore; flowers fade in autumn at the Han palace."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before long Lady Peng, the Lady of Qin, died. Wenzhao mourned and ordered literary men to compose elegies; Wendde submitted more than ten pieces, one couplet reading, "The moon sinks cold at the Xiang shore; flowers fade in autumn at the Han palace."

manualTranslations.zh: 文昭覽之大驚，曰：「文德有此作用，吾但以寢陋而輕之，乃不如南宮小兒卻能知賢耶！」
manualTranslations.literal: Wenzhao read them and was greatly startled, saying: "Wendde has such talent—I only slighted him for being homely, yet I am not even the equal of that Southern Residence lad in knowing worth!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wenzhao was astonished and said, "Wendde has such talent—I only slighted him for his looks, yet I am not even the equal of that Southern Residence lad in recognizing worth!"

manualTranslations.zh: 於是始召文德而愧謝之。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he at last summoned Wendde and apologized in shame.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then summoned Wendde and apologized in shame.

manualTranslations.zh: 未幾，承制授水部員外郎，充融州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: Before long, by imperial commission, he was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and served as prefect of Rongzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before long he was commissioned Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and appointed prefect of Rongzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 文德晚尤好著述，乃撰《大唐新纂》十三卷，多名人遺事，詞雖不工，事或可采，時以多聞許之。
manualTranslations.literal: In his later years Wendde especially loved writing and compiled the New Compendium of the Great Tang in thirteen scrolls, containing many anecdotes of famous men; though the style was not polished, the material was worth collecting, and people of the time acknowledged him as widely learned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In his later years Wendde especially loved writing and compiled the New Compendium of the Great Tang in thirteen scrolls, containing many anecdotes of famous men; though the style was not polished, the material was worth collecting, and contemporaries acknowledged him as widely learned.

manualTranslations.literal: Once enfeoffed as King of Chu, he still asked to follow the Tang precedent of princely field headquarters, establishing a full staff of heavenly offices with the title Literary Garden Academician and authority over edicts and orders; he controlled more than twenty prefectures, appointed officials himself, withheld tax payments, and monopolized the purchase of tea gathered among the people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once enfeoffed King of Chu, he still asked to follow the Tang precedent of princely field headquarters, establishing a full staff with Literary Garden Academicians and authority over edicts; he controlled more than twenty prefectures, appointed officials himself, withheld taxes, and monopolized tea gathered among the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 又自鑄鉛鐵錢，凡天下商賈所賫寶貨入其境者，只以土產鉛鐵博易之無餘，遂致一方富盛，窮極奢侈，貢奉朝廷不過茶數萬斤而已。
manualTranslations.literal: He also cast his own lead and iron coinage; whatever treasure goods merchants from all the realm brought into his territory were exchanged only for local lead and iron until nothing remained, so that one region grew rich and extravagance reached its limit, while tribute to the court amounted to no more than several tens of thousands of jin of tea.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also cast his own lead and iron coinage; whatever treasure merchants brought into his territory was exchanged only for local lead and iron until nothing remained, making the region rich and extravagance extreme, while tribute to the court amounted to no more than several tens of thousands of jin of tea.

manualTranslations.zh: 於中原賣茶之利，歲百萬計。
manualTranslations.literal: The profit from selling tea in the Central Plains amounted to a million each year.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Profits from selling tea in the Central Plains ran to a million a year.

manualTranslations.zh: 唐同光初，首修職貢，復授太師、兼尚書令、楚王。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang of Tang he first restored official tribute and was again given Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and King of Chu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tang Tongguang he first restored official tribute and was again given Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and King of Chu.

manualTranslations.zh: 天成初，加守尚書令。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was further made Acting Director of the Secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was further made Acting Director of the Secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 長興二年十一月十日，薨於位，時年七十有八。
manualTranslations.literal: On the tenth day of the eleventh month of the second year of Changxing he died in office, aged seventy-eight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the eleventh month of Changxing 2 he died in office at the age of seventy-eight.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗聞之，廢朝三日，謚曰武穆。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong heard of it he suspended court for three days and gave the posthumous title Wumu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingzong heard of it he suspended court for three days and gave the posthumous title Wumu.

manualTranslations.zh: 子希聲嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Xisheng succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Xisheng succeeded him.

sourceRange.text: 十八年，渭死，溫聞之，自金陵馳歸揚州，夜入廣陵，議有所立。或有希溫旨，言及蜀先主遺命諸葛亮之事，溫厲聲曰：「若楊氏無男，有女當立矣，無得異議。」由是群心乃定，遂迎丹陽王溥於潤州，以其年六月十八日即偽位，改元為順義。自是溫父子愈盛，中外共專其國，楊氏主祭而已。溫累官至竭忠定難建國功臣、大丞相、都督中外諸軍事、諸道都統、鎮海寧國等軍節度、宣歙池等州管內營田觀察等使、開府儀同三司、守太師、中書令、金陵尹、東海王，食邑一萬戶，實封五百戶。偽順義七年改乾貞元年，即後唐天成二年。其年十月二十三日，溫卒，偽贈大元帥，追封齊王，謚曰忠武。

context.beforeSource: 明年，溫冊楊渭為天子，僭稱大吳，改唐天祐十六年為武義元年。
context.afterSource: 昪前夢溫負登山，逾年溫卒，昪乃偽授輔政興邦功臣，知內外左右事、開府儀同三同、守太尉、中書令、宣城公。

manualTranslations.literal: In the eighteenth year Wei died; when Wen heard of it he galloped from Jinling back to Yangzhou, entered Guangling by night, and deliberated on whom to enthrone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Yang Wei died. When Xu Wen heard the news, he galloped from Jinling back to Yangzhou, entered Guangling by night, and debated whom to put on the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 或有希溫旨，言及蜀先主遺命諸葛亮之事，溫厲聲曰：「若楊氏無男，有女當立矣，無得異議。」
manualTranslations.literal: Some who hoped to please Wen's intent spoke of the Former Lord of Shu's deathbed command to Zhuge Liang; Wen said sternly: "If the Yang house has no son, a daughter should be enthroned — no dissent will be tolerated."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some, hoping to curry favor with Xu Wen, brought up the Shu Former Lord's deathbed charge to Zhuge Liang. Wen snapped, "If the Yang house has no son, a daughter may be enthroned — and there will be no debate."

manualTranslations.zh: 由是群心乃定，遂迎丹陽王溥於潤州，以其年六月十八日即偽位，改元為順義。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon the minds of the multitude were settled; they thereupon welcomed the Prince of Danyang, Pu, at Runzhou, and on the eighteenth day of the sixth month of that year he assumed the false throne and changed the era name to Shunyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With that the court settled. They brought Yang Pu, Prince of Danyang, to Runzhou, and on the eighteenth day of the sixth month he took the throne and adopted the era name Shunyi.

manualTranslations.zh: 自是溫父子愈盛，中外共專其國，楊氏主祭而已。
manualTranslations.literal: From this time the Wen father and sons grew ever more powerful; within and without they jointly monopolized the state, and the Yang clan performed sacrifices only.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From then on the Wen father and sons grew ever stronger and ran the realm inside and out, while the Yang clan performed rites and little else.

manualTranslations.zh: 溫累官至竭忠定難建國功臣、大丞相、都督中外諸軍事、諸道都統、鎮海寧國等軍節度、宣歙池等州管內營田觀察等使、開府儀同三司、守太師、中書令、金陵尹、東海王，食邑一萬戶，實封五百戶。
manualTranslations.literal: Wen rose in office to Merit Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty, Quells Disturbance, and Builds the State, Grand Chancellor, commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, overall commander of all circuits, military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo and other armies, commissioner of farming and observation within Xuan, She, Chi, and other prefectures, Bearer of the Golden Bellow and Grand Preceptor of the Palace, Acting Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, chief administrator of Jinling, Prince of Donghai, with a fief of ten thousand households and an actual enfeoffment of five hundred households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xu Wen rose to Merit Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty, Quells Disturbance, and Builds the State, Grand Chancellor, supreme commander of all armies, overall commander of all circuits, military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo, farming and observation commissioner for Xuan, She, Chi, and neighboring prefectures, Bearer of the Golden Bellow, Acting Grand Preceptor, Secretariat Director, chief administrator of Jinling, and Prince of Donghai, with a nominal fief of ten thousand households and a substantive enfeoffment of five hundred.

manualTranslations.zh: 偽順義七年改乾貞元年，即後唐天成二年。
manualTranslations.literal: In the false state, the seventh year of Shunyi was changed to the first year of Qianzhen, which was the second year of Later Tang Tiancheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Shunyi the Wu court changed the era to Qianzhen 1, the same year as Later Tang Tiancheng 2.

manualTranslations.zh: 其年十月二十三日，溫卒，偽贈大元帥，追封齊王，謚曰忠武。
manualTranslations.literal: That year, on the twenty-third day of the tenth month, Wen died; in the false state he was posthumously invested as Grand Marshal, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Qi, and given the posthumous title Zhongwu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year, on the twenty-third day of the tenth month, Xu Wen died. The Wu court posthumously made him Grand Marshal, enfeoffed him as Prince of Qi, and gave him the posthumous title Zhongwu.

manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Qianhua under Liang, commissioner Zhou Yiyan and others were sent to court with tribute. Emperor Taizu received them in audience at Chaoyuan Hall. Yiyan was made Acting Right General-in-Chief of the Right Gate Guard, Shi Shou'er and Shi Lunci were both made Acting Generals of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and Left Gate Guard General Yang Zhao was appointed envoy to escort the Uyghurs home. The Five Dynasties Essentials records: Yiyan was made Acting Right General-in-Chief of the Right Gate Guard; his younger brother Luemaizhi and Shi Lunci were both made Acting Generals of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard; Li Wuzhu and An Yanshan were both made Acting Generals of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard; and Left Gate Guard Senior General Yang Zhao was made Senior General of the Left Xiaowei Guard and appointed envoy to escort the Uyghurs home.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Qianhua under Liang, commissioner Zhou Yiyan and others came to court with tribute. Emperor Taizu received them in audience at Chaoyuan Hall, appointing Yiyan Acting Right General-in-Chief of the Right Gate Guard, Shi Shou'er and Shi Lunci Acting Generals of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and Left Gate Guard General Yang Zhao envoy to escort the Uyghurs home. The Five Dynasties Essentials gives a fuller account: Yiyan as Acting Right General-in-Chief of the Right Gate Guard; his younger brother Luemaizhi and Shi Lunci as Acting Generals of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard; Li Wuzhu and An Yanshan as Acting Generals of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard; and Senior General Yang Zhao of the Left Gate Guard as Senior General of the Left Xiaowei Guard and envoy to escort the Uyghurs home.

sourceRange.text: 周廣順元年二月，遣使並摩尼貢玉團七十有七，白絺、貂皮、犛牛尾、藥物等。先是，晉、漢已來，回鶻每至京師，禁民以私市易，其所有寶貨皆鬻之入官，民間市易者罪之。至是，周太祖命除去舊法，每回鶻來者，聽私下交易，官中不得禁詰，由是玉之價直十損七八。顯德六年二月，又遣使朝貢，獻玉並碙砂等物，皆不納，所入馬量給價錢。時世宗以玉雖稱寶，無益國用，故因而卻之。

manualTranslations.zh: 周廣順元年二月，遣使並摩尼貢玉團七十有七，白絺、貂皮、犛牛尾、藥物等。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Guangshun under Zhou, envoys together with the Manichaean mission presented seventy-seven jade balls, white silk, sable pelts, yak tails, medicines, and the like.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Guangshun under Zhou, envoys came with the Manichaean mission bearing seventy-seven jade balls, white silk, sable pelts, yak tails, medicines, and other goods.

manualTranslations.zh: 先是，晉、漢已來，回鶻每至京師，禁民以私市易，其所有寶貨皆鬻之入官，民間市易者罪之。
manualTranslations.literal: Previously, from Jin and Han onward, whenever the Uyghurs reached the capital private trade with the populace was forbidden; all their valuables had to be sold to the government, and private traders were punished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Previously, from the Jin and Han dynasties onward, whenever Uyghur missions reached the capital the people were forbidden to trade with them privately. All their valuables had to be sold to the government, and anyone who traded privately was punished.

manualTranslations.zh: 至是，周太祖命除去舊法，每回鶻來者，聽私下交易，官中不得禁詰，由是玉之價直十損七八。
manualTranslations.literal: At this point Emperor Taizu of Zhou ordered the old regulations abolished: whenever Uyghurs came, private trade was permitted and officials might not prohibit or interrogate them; from this the price of jade fell by seven or eight tenths.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereupon Emperor Taizu of Zhou abolished the old rules. Whenever Uyghurs came, private trade was allowed and officials were forbidden to interfere. As a result the price of jade fell by seven or eight tenths.

manualTranslations.zh: 顯德六年二月，又遣使朝貢，獻玉並碙砂等物，皆不納，所入馬量給價錢。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Xiande they again sent envoys to court, presenting jade, ammoniac, and other goods; all were refused, and for horses brought in payment was given by measure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year of Xiande they sent envoys again with jade, ammoniac, and other goods. The court refused them all and paid only for the horses they accepted.

manualTranslations.zh: 時世宗以玉雖稱寶，無益國用，故因而卻之。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Emperor Shizong held that although jade was called a treasure, it did not benefit state needs, and therefore rejected it on that account.

sourceRange.text: 清泰末年，末帝先人墳側古佛剎中石像，忽然搖動不已，觀者咸訝焉。晉開運元年七月一日，少帝御明德門，宣赦改元。是日，遇大雷雨，門內有井亭，亭有石盆，有走水槽，槽有龍首，其夕悉飄行數十步，而龍首斷焉。識者曰：「石，國姓也，此兆非祥，石氏其遷乎！其絕乎！」二年正月，汴州封丘門外，壕水東北隅水上有文，若大樹花葉芬敷之狀，相連數十株，宛若圖畫，傾都觀之。識者云：「唐景福中，盧彥威浮陽壕水有樹文亦如此，時有高尼辭郡人曰：『此地當有兵難。』至光化中，其郡果為燕帥劉仁恭所陷。」三年九月，大水，太原葭蘆茂盛，最上一葉如旗狀，皆南指。十二月己丑，雨木冰。是月戊戌，霜霧大降，草木皆如冰。

manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Qingtai, at an ancient Buddhist monastery beside the tomb of the Last Emperor's forebears, a stone image suddenly shook without cease; all who viewed it were astonished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Qingtai era, a stone image in an ancient Buddhist monastery beside the tomb of the Last Emperor's ancestors suddenly began to shake without cease, astonishing all who saw it.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month of the first year of Kaiyun of Later Jin, the Young Emperor appeared at Mingde Gate, proclaimed an amnesty, and changed the reign title.

manualTranslations.zh: 是日，遇大雷雨，門內有井亭，亭有石盆，有走水槽，槽有龍首，其夕悉飄行數十步，而龍首斷焉。
manualTranslations.literal: That day a great thunderstorm struck. Inside the gate was a well pavilion; the pavilion had a stone basin, the basin had a running-water channel, and the channel had a dragon head. That evening all drifted several tens of paces, and the dragon head broke off.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That day a violent thunderstorm struck. Inside the gate stood a well pavilion with a stone basin and a running-water channel bearing a dragon head. That evening all were swept several dozen paces, and the dragon head broke off.

manualTranslations.zh: 識者曰：「石，國姓也，此兆非祥，石氏其遷乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Those with insight said: "Stone is the dynastic surname; this omen is not auspicious. Will the Shi clan be displaced?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those versed in omens said, "Stone is the dynastic surname. This omen is not auspicious. Will the Shi clan be displaced?

manualTranslations.zh: 其絕乎！」
manualTranslations.literal: Or will it be cut off?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Or will it be cut off?"

manualTranslations.literal: In the first month of the second year, outside Fengqiu Gate in Bian Prefecture, on the water at the northeast corner of the moat there appeared patterns like great trees with flowers and leaves in full bloom, linked in several tens of clumps like a painted picture; the whole capital turned out to view them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, outside Fengqiu Gate in Bian Prefecture, patterns appeared on the water at the northeast corner of the moat like great trees in full bloom, linked in dozens of clusters like a painted scroll. manualTranslations.zh: 識者云：「唐景福中，盧彥威浮陽壕水有樹文亦如此，時有高尼辭郡人曰：『此地當有兵難。』
manualTranslations.literal: Those with insight said: "In Jingfu of Tang, Lu Yanwei's Fuyang moat water also had tree patterns like this. At the time a lofty nun took leave of the people of the commandery, saying: 'This place will suffer military calamity.'"

manualTranslations.zh: 至光化中，其郡果為燕帥劉仁恭所陷。」

manualTranslations.idiomatic: By the Guanghua era that commandery was indeed overrun by the Yan commander Liu Rengong."

manualTranslations.zh: 三年九月，大水，太原葭蘆茂盛，最上一葉如旗狀，皆南指。

sourceRange.text: 」長興元年夏，鄜州上言，大水入城，居人溺死。三年四月，棣州上言，水壞其城。是月己巳，鄆州上言，黃河水溢岸，闊三十里，東流。五月丁亥，申州奏大水，平地深七尺。是月戊申，襄州上言，漢水溢入城，壞民廬舍，又壞均州郛郭，水深三丈，居民登山避水，仍畫圖以進。是月甲子，洛水溢，壞民廬舍。六月壬戌，汴州上言，大雨，雷震文宣王廟講堂。十一月壬子，鄆州上言，黃河暴漲，漂溺四千餘戶。三年七月，諸州大水，宋、亳、潁尤甚。宰臣奏曰：「今秋宋州管界，水災最盛，人戶流亡，栗價暴貴。臣等商量，請於本州倉出斛斗，依時出糶，以救貧民。」從之。是月，秦州大水，溺死窯谷內居民三十六人。夔州赤甲山崩，大水漂溺居人。

context.beforeSource: 應在京及諸縣，有停貯斛斗，並令減價出糶，以濟公私，如不遵守，仰具聞奏。
context.afterSource: 清泰元年九月，連雨害稼。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year Di Prefecture reported that floodwaters destroyed its city walls.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: That month, on the jisi day, Yan Prefecture reported that the Yellow River overflowed its banks to a breadth of thirty li and flowed eastward.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月丁亥，申州奏大水，平地深七尺。
manualTranslations.literal: On the dinghai day of the fifth month, Shen Prefecture memorialized great flooding; on level ground the water stood seven chi deep.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the fifth month Shen Prefecture reported severe flooding, with water seven chi deep across the flatlands.

manualTranslations.zh: 是月戊申，襄州上言，漢水溢入城，壞民廬舍，又壞均州郛郭，水深三丈，居民登山避水，仍畫圖以進。
manualTranslations.literal: That month, on the wushen day, Xiang Prefecture reported upward that the Han River overflowed into the city, destroying commoners' houses; it also destroyed the outer walls of Jun Prefecture. The water stood three zhang deep; residents climbed mountains to escape the water and still painted diagrams to submit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That month, on the wushen day, Xiang Prefecture reported that the Han River surged into the city and destroyed houses, and also breached the outer walls of Jun Prefecture. manualTranslations.zh: 是月甲子，洛水溢，壞民廬舍。
manualTranslations.literal: That month, on the jiazi day, the Luo River overflowed and destroyed commoners' houses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That month, on the jiazi day, the Luo River overflowed and destroyed houses.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the renxu day of the sixth month Bian Prefecture reported heavy rain and thunder that struck the lecture hall of the Temple of King Wenxuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一月壬子，鄆州上言，黃河暴漲，漂溺四千餘戶。
manualTranslations.literal: On the renzi day of the eleventh month, Yan Prefecture reported upward that the Yellow River rose violently, sweeping away and drowning more than four thousand households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the eleventh month Yan Prefecture reported that the Yellow River rose violently, sweeping away and drowning more than four thousand households.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年七月，諸州大水，宋、亳、潁尤甚。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year many prefectures were inundated, Song, Bo, and Ying most severely.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣等商量，請於本州倉出斛斗，依時出糶，以救貧民。」
manualTranslations.literal: We have deliberated and request that grain be taken from this prefecture's granaries and sold at the proper season to relieve the poor."

manualTranslations.zh: 從之。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

manualTranslations.literal: That month, Qin Prefecture suffered great flooding; thirty-six residents within Yaogu were drowned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That same month Qin Prefecture was inundated, drowning thirty-six residents in Yaogu.

manualTranslations.zh: 夔州赤甲山崩，大水漂溺居人。

二月，太常埔士段颙議曰：夫宗廟之制，歷代為難，須考禮經，以求故事。謹按《尚書·舜典》曰：「正月上日，受終於文祖。此是堯之廟也，猶未載其數。又按《郊祀錄》曰：夏立五廟，商立六廟，周立七廟。漢初立祖宗廟於郡國，共計一百六十七所。後漢光武中興後，別立六廟。魏明帝初立親廟四，後重議依周法立七廟。晉武帝受禪，初立六廟，後復立七廟。宋武帝初立六廟，齊朝亦立六廟。隋文帝受命，初立親廟四，至大業元年，煬帝欲遵周法，議立七廟。次屬傳禪於唐，武德元年六月四日，始立四廟於長安，至貞觀九年，命有司詳議廟制，遂立七廟，至開元十一年後，創立九廟。又按《禮記·喪服小記》曰：「王者禘其祖之所自出，以其祖配之，而立四廟。鄭玄註云：高祖巳下至禰四世，即親盡也，更立始祖為不遷之廟，共五廟也。又按《禮記·祭法》及《王制》、《孔子家語》、《春秋穀梁傳》並云：天子七廟，諸侯五廟，大夫三廟，士一廟。此是降殺以兩之義。又按《尚書·咸有一德》曰：「七世之廟，可以觀德。又按《疑義》云：天子立七廟，或四廟，蓋有其義也。如四廟者，從禰至高祖已下親盡，故有四廟之理。又立七廟者，緣自古聖王，祖有功，宗有德，更封立始祖，即於四親廟之外，或祖功宗德，不拘定數，所以有五廟、六廟，或七廟、九廟，欲後代子孫觀其功德，故《尚書》云「七世之廟，可以觀德」矣。又按周舍論云：「自江左已來，晉、宋、齊、梁相承，多立七廟。今臣等參詳，唯立七廟，即並通其理。伏緣宗廟事大，不敢執以一理定之，故檢七廟、四廟二件之文，俱得其宜，他所論者，並皆勿取。請下三省集百官詳議。敕旨宜依。左僕射劉句等議曰：臣等今月八日，伏奉敕命於尚書省集議太常博士段颙所議宗廟事。伏以將敷至化，以達萬方，克致平和，必先宗廟。故《禮記·王制》云：「天子七廟，諸侯五廟，大夫三廟。疏云：「周制之七者，太祖廟及文王、武王之祧，與親廟四。太祖，後稷也。商六廟，契及湯與二昭、二穆。夏則五廟，無太祖，禹與二昭、二穆而已。自夏及周，少不減五，多不過七。又云：「天子七廟，皆據周也。有其人則七，無其人則五。若諸侯廟制，雖有其人，則不過五。此則天子、諸侯七、五之異明矣。至於三代已後魏、晉、宋、齊、隋及唐初，多立六廟或四廟，蓋於建國之始，不盈七廟之數也。今欲請立自高祖已下四親廟，其始祖一廟，未敢輕議，伏俟聖裁。御史中丞張昭遠奏議曰：臣前月中預都省集議宗廟事，伏見議狀於親廟之外，請別立始祖一廟，近奏中書門下牒，再令百官於都省議定聞奏者。臣讀十四代史書，見二千年故事，觀諸家宗廟，都無始祖之稱，唯商、周二代，以稷、契為太祖。《禮記》曰：「天子七廟，三昭、三穆，與太祖之廟而七。鄭玄註：「此周制也。七者，太祖後稷及文王、武王與四親廟。又曰：「商人六廟，契及成湯與二昭、二穆也。夏後氏立五廟，不立太祖，惟禹與二昭、二穆而已。據《王制》鄭玄所釋，即商、周以稷、契為太祖，夏後無太祖，亦無追謚之廟。自商、周以來，時更十代，皆於親廟之中，以有功者為太祖，無追崇始祖之例。具引今古，即恐詞繁，事要證明，須陳梗概。漢以高祖父太上皇執嘉無社稷功，不立廟號，高帝自為高祖。魏以曹公相漢，垂三十年，始封於魏，故為太祖。晉以宣王輔魏有功，立為高祖，以景帝始封晉，故為太祖。宋氏先世，官閥卑微，雖追崇帝號，劉裕自為高祖。南齊高帝之父，位至右將軍，生無封爵，不得為太祖，高帝自為太祖。梁武帝父順之，佐佑齊室，封侯，位至領軍、丹陽尹，雖不受封於梁，亦為太祖。陳武帝父文贊，生無名位，以武帝功，梁室贈侍中，封義興公，及武帝即位，亦追為太祖。周閔帝以父泰相西魏，經營王業，始封於周，故為太祖。隋文帝父忠，輔周室有大功，始封於隋，故為太祖。唐高祖神堯祖父虎為周八柱國，隋代追封唐公，故為太祖。唐末梁室朱氏有帝位，亦立四廟，朱公先世無名位，雖追冊四廟，不立太祖，朱公自為太祖。此則前代追冊太祖，不出親廟之成例也。王者祖有功而宗有德，漢、魏之制，非有功德不得立為祖宗，商、周受命，以稷、契有大功於唐、虞之際，故追尊為太祖。自秦、漢之後，其禮不然，雖祖有功，仍須親廟。今亦粗言往例，以取證明。秦稱造父之後，不以造父為始祖；漢稱唐堯、劉累之後，不以堯、累為始祖；魏稱曹參之後，不以參為始祖；晉稱趙將司馬卬之後，不以卬為始祖；宋稱漢楚元王之後，不以元王為始祖；齊、梁皆稱蕭何之後，不以蕭何為始祖；陳稱太丘長陳寔之後，不以實為始祖；元魏稱李陵之後，不以陵為始祖；後周稱神農之後，不以神農為始祖；隋稱楊震之後，不以楊震為始祖；唐稱臯陶、老子之後，不以臯陶、老子為始祖。唯唐高宗則天武後臨朝，革唐稱周，又立七廟，仍追冊周文王姬昌為始祖，此蓋當時附麗之徒，不諳故實，武立姬廟，乖越已甚，曲臺之人，到今嗤誚。臣遠觀秦、漢，下至周、隋，禮樂衣冠，聲明文物，未有如唐室之盛。武德議廟之初，英才間出，如溫、魏、顏、虞通今古，封、蕭、薛、杜達禮儀，制度憲章，必有師法。夫追崇先王、先母之儀，起於周代。據《史記》及禮經云：「武王纘太王、王季、文王之緒，一戎衣而有天下，尊為天子，宗廟饗之。周公成文、武之德，追王太王、王季，祀先公以天子之禮。又曰「郊祀後稷以配天。據此言之，周武雖祀七世，追為王號者，但四世而已。故自東漢以來，有國之初，多崇四廟，從周制也。況商因夏禮，漢習秦儀，無勞博訪之文，宜約已成之制。請依隋、唐有國之初，創立四廟，推四世之中名位高者為太祖。謹議以聞。敕：宜令尚書省集百官，將前議狀與張昭遠所陳，速定奪聞奏。左僕射劉句等再議奏曰：臣等今月十三日，再於尚書省集百官詳議。夫王者祖武宗文，郊天祀地，故有追崇之典，以申配饗之儀。初詳太常禮院議狀，唯立七廟四廟，即並通其理。其他所論，並皆勿取。七廟者，按《禮記·王制》曰：「天子七廟，三昭、三穆與太祖之廟而七。鄭玄註云：「此周制也。詳其禮經，即是周家七廟之定數。四廟者，謂高、曾、祖、禰四世也。按《周本紀》及《禮記·大傳》皆曰：「武王即位，追王太王、王季、文王。以後稷為堯稷官，故追尊為太祖。此即周武王初有天下，追尊四廟之明文也。故自嘆、魏已降，迄於周、隋，創業之君，追謚不過四世，約周制也。此禮行之已久，事在不疑。今參詳都省前議狀，請立四廟外，別引始祖，取裁未為定議。續準敕據御史中丞張昭遠奏，請創立四廟之外，無別封始祖之文。況國家禮樂刑名，皆依唐典，宗廟之制，須約舊章。請依唐朝追尊獻祖宣皇帝、懿祖光皇帝、太祖景皇帝、代祖元皇帝故事，追尊四廟為定」從之。

sourceRange.text: 五年，始議重興二舞，詔曰：「」其年秋，棁等具述制度上奏云：從之。

localRange.text: 五年，始議重興二舞，詔曰：「正冬二節，朝會舊儀，廢於離亂之時，興自和平之代。將期備物，全系用心；須議擇人，同為定制。其正冬朝會禮節、樂章、二舞行列等事宜，差太常卿崔棁、御史中丞竇貞固、刑部侍郎呂琦、禮部侍郎張允與太常寺官一一詳定。禮從新意，道在舊章，庶知治世之和，漸見移風之善。其年秋，棁等具述制度上奏云：案《禮》云：「天子以德為車，以樂為禦。「大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。又曰：「安上治民，莫善於禮；移風易俗，莫善於樂。故樂書議舞云：夫樂在耳曰聲，在目曰容。聲應乎耳，可以聽知；容藏於心，難以貌睹。故聖人假幹戚羽旄以表其容，發揚蹈厲以見其意，聲容和合，則大樂備矣。又案《義鏡》，問鼓吹十二案合於何所？答云：《周禮》鼓人掌六鼓四金，漢朝乃有黃門鼓吹。崔豹《古今註》云：因張騫使西域，得《摩訶兜勒》一曲，李延年增之，分為二十八曲。梁置鼓吹清商令二人。唐又有堈鼓、金鉦、大鼓、長鳴、歌簫、笳、笛，合為鼓吹十二案，大享會則設於懸外。此乃是設二舞及鼓吹十二案之由也。今議一從令式，排列教習。文舞郎六十四人，分為八佾，每佾八人。左手執籥。《禮》云：「葦籥，伊耆氏之樂也。《周禮》有「籥師教國子」，《爾雅》曰：籥如笛，三孔而短，大者七孔，謂之簅。歷代已來，文舞所用，凡用籥六十有四。右手執翟，《周禮》所謂羽舞也。《書》云：「舞幹羽於兩階。翟，山雉也，以雉羽公析連攢而為之。二人執纛前引，數於舞人之外。舞人冠進賢冠，服黃紗袍，白紗中單，皂領褾，白練衤蓋襠，白布大口袴，革帶，烏皮履，白布襪。武舞郎六十四人，分為八佾。左手執幹。幹，楯也，今之旁牌，所以翳身也，其色赤，中畫獸形，故謂之朱幹。《周禮》所謂兵舞，取其武象，用楯六十有四。右手執戚。戚，斧也，上飾以玉，故謂之玉戚。二人執旌前引，旌似旗而小，絳色，畫升龍。二人執鼗鼓，二人執鐸。《周禮》有四金之奏，其三曰金鐸，以通鼓，形如大鈴，仰而振之。金錞二，每錞二人舉之，一人奏之。《周禮》四金之奏，一曰金錞，以和鼓，銅鑄為之，其色黑，其形圓，若椎，上大下小，高三尺六寸有六分，圍二尺四寸，上有伏虎之狀，旁有耳，獸形銜镮。二人執鐃以次之。《周禮》四金之奏，二曰金鐃，以止鼓，如鈴無舌，搖柄以鳴之。二人掌相在左，《禮》云：「治亂以相。制如小鼓，用皮為表，實之以糠，撫之以節樂。二人掌雅在右，《禮》云：「訊疾以雅。以木為之，狀如漆筒而弇口，大二尺圍，長五尺六寸，以羖皮鞔之，旁有二紐，髹畫，賓醉而出，以器築地，明行不失節。武舞人服弁，平巾幘，金支緋絲大袖，緋絲布裲襠，甲金飾，白練𧞔襠，錦騰蛇起梁帶，豹文大口布袴，烏皮靴。工人二十，數於舞人之外。武弁朱翙，革帶，烏皮履，白練礻蓋襠，白布襪。殿庭仍加鼓吹十二案。《義鏡》云：常設氈案，以氈為床也。今請制大床十二，慶容九人，振作歌樂，其床為熊羆貙豹騰倚之狀以承之，象百獸率舞之意。分置於建鼓之外，各三案，每案羽葆鼓一，大鼓一，金錞一，歌二人，簫二人，笳二人。十二案，樂工百有八人，舞郎一百三十有二人，取年十五已上，弱冠已下，容止端正者。其歌曲名號、樂章詞句，中書條奏，差官修撰。從之。
